title: Director of Implementation
description:
About Doctronic

Doctronic is the #1 AI doctor. Our AI is free, anonymous and HIPAA-compliant, and it has delivered over 30 million consults to date. In December 2025 we became the first and only AI legally authorized to practice medicine, renewing prescriptions autonomously under Utah's AI Learning Lab, and the first AI ever granted medical malpractice insurance. We are live in all 50 states and DC with AI and human physicians available 24/7, and we have raised $65M through our Series B from Abstract, Lightspeed, Union Square Ventures and others.

We are now building the enterprise organization that takes this to health plans, health systems and the wider healthcare ecosystem. This role owns everything that happens after a partner signs.

The Role

Every signed partnership goes live on time, at quality, without engineering heroics. That is the whole mandate.

We have live partners today and more in build, and we have learned the hard way that launch quality currently depends too much on who happens to be assigned. You will fix that: build the delivery pods, build the repeatable launch process, and own the launch date. Your primary metric is on-time launch rate, with a target of moving signature to go-live under 60 days.

You will report to the Chief Business Officer and lead a team of deployment strategists and solutions engineers, growing to three pods. You will also be the escalation path for partners, which today defaults to engineering and should not.

What You'll Do

  • Own the launch of every enterprise partnership from signature to go-live, across co-branded deployments, embedded chat and API integrations

  • Build and lead delivery pods, each pairing a deployment strategist who owns the plan and the partner relationship with one to two solutions engineers

  • Own the requirements document and hold the line on scope. If a partner asks for something new, it goes to the deal desk and product, not into the build

  • Own the technical service level agreement and the delivery commitments we make in every statement of work, including before signature

  • Stand up the launch playbook: internal kickoff at 80% closed, external kickoff, build, QA, clinical readiness, go-live, and the 30-day retro

  • Run the handoff from sales, and make sure nobody walks into a partner kickoff without having read the statement of work

  • Partner with our Enterprise Product Lead on the bespoke versus platform call, and drive the share of partner requirements we can meet with existing product upward every quarter

  • Own the reuse verdict after each launch: template it, productize it, or retire it

  • Be the escalation path, so that engineering can build instead of firefight

What We're Looking For

  • 8+ years in implementation, professional services, technical program management or solutions delivery, including 3+ years managing people

  • Has delivered technical integrations into regulated enterprises: health systems, payers, pharmacy, or financial services

  • Technically fluent. APIs, webhooks, SSO, and healthcare data standards such as FHIR. You can hold your own with engineers and be useful in the conversation

  • Has told a customer no and kept the relationship. This is the single most important thing we are screening for

  • Has built process where none existed, rather than administered process someone else designed

  • Writes clearly and runs a meeting well. Most of the failure modes in this job are communication failures

  • Based in New York City or willing to relocate. This is a hybrid role

Nice to Have

  • FHIR R4, HL7, or direct Epic or Cerner integration experience

  • Has run a pod, squad or forward-deployed engineering model

  • Telehealth or clinical workflow delivery experience

  • Experience introducing self-service tooling or a partner portal to reduce manual onboarding

  • Has owned a technical SLA and the support tiering behind it

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base salary range: $225-$250k + equity

  • Health reimbursement allowance, support for well-being, and flexible time off

title: Principal Architect (Customer & Revenue Transformation)
description:
This role owns learn, shop, buy, catalog, marketing, sales, CRM and ordering, plus quote-to-cash and AI-enabled engagement. The front-office architect.


GCI's Principal Architect will define, communicate, govern, and advance architecture direction in support of business outcomes, technology modernization, operational effectiveness, and long-term organizational objectives. These roles partner with business, product, engineering, delivery, operations, and leadership stakeholders to translate organizational needs into sustainable solutions, standards, roadmaps, and technology capabilities. The job family provides architectural leadership across products, platforms, systems, services, and business capabilities by developing guidance, patterns, target-state designs, and roadmaps that reduce complexity, manage risk, improve agility, and optimize technology investments. Roles apply common architecture principles, governance practices, and industry standards across one or more architecture practice areas, with scope, autonomy, and decision influence increasing by career level.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Assess business objectives, customer needs, operational priorities, current-state capabilities, technologies, processes, operating models, risks, dependencies, architecture gaps, technical debt, lifecycle risks, and modernization opportunities.
  • Develop target-state architectures, transition states, and roadmaps that guide technology investment, solution design, and implementation planning.
  • Create architecture artifacts, models, standards, patterns, reference designs, principles, non-functional requirements, and design guardrails; evaluate alternatives and recommend fit-for-purpose solutions.
  • Participate in architecture reviews and governance forums, applying architecture standards, policies, principles, and industry practices.
  • Manage architecture risks, dependencies, technical debt, lifecycle considerations, exceptions, reusable assets, repositories, and technology rationalization efforts.
  • Partner with product, delivery, engineering, and operations teams to provide architecture guidance through planning, design, delivery, and operationalization.
  • Support road mapping, dependency management, implementation sequencing, decision facilitation, trade-off discussions, and alignment to intended architecture outcomes.
  • Improve architecture methods, tools, standards, governance practices, operating models, reusable patterns, communities of practice, mentoring, knowledge sharing, innovation, and simplification.

Discipline-Specific Focus Areas:

The core responsibilities and minimum qualifications outlined in this job description apply across the Architect job family. Discipline-specific responsibilities, technical competencies, and/or preferred qualifications are defined in the applicable addendum. See the corresponding discipline-specific addendum for additional details.

Enterprise Architecture:

Defines enterprise-wide business and technology direction, target-state architecture, capability alignment, governance standards, portfolio strategy, and technology roadmaps. Provides strategic guidance to align investments, modernization, and architecture decisions with long-term organizational objectives.

Business Architecture:

Defines business capabilities, value streams, operating model impacts, business process alignment, organizational dependencies, and business architecture views that connect strategy to execution.

Solution Architecture:

Defines solution direction, design, standards, and roadmaps for business initiatives and technology solutions. Provides guidance to align business needs with scalable, secure, supportable solutions while balancing value, cost, risk, complexity, and long-term sustainability.

Minimum Qualifications:

Career Level:

Recognized organizational authority; sets long-term architecture strategy, principles, and technical direction.

Provides advanced technical and architectural leadership across complex initiatives. Defines and forecasts architecture requirements, drives platform and enterprise capability growth, and serves as a senior consulting resource.

  • Lead complex architecture initiatives and guide cross-functional teams.
  • Define current- and future-state architecture requirements and roadmaps.
  • Provide expert consulting and strategic recommendations to resolve complex challenges.
  • Participate in setting architectural direction and advise on enterprise strategy and development.
  • Develop and enhance architecture documentation, templates, standards, principles, policies, and guidelines.
  • Mentor architects and technical staff and review architecture/design deliverables.

REQUIRED:

* A combination of education and relevant work experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties of the position may substitute to meet the total years required on a year-for-year basis.

Education*:

  • High school diploma or equivalent; this requirement is met by candidates who hold an associate or bachelor’s degree.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Business, Data Management, Cybersecurity, or related discipline.

Experience*:

  • Minimum of 10 years of relevant experience, including experience in at least two relevant architecture/technology disciplines.
  • Typical scope: Organization. Primary differentiator: Organizational Influence.

Skills:

Guides technology strategy, portfolio alignment, architecture governance, and professional capability development. Influences executive decision-making, investment prioritization, and organization-wide architectural direction. Demonstrated proficiency appropriate to level in: Architecture modeling and documentation; business and technology alignment; systems design and integration; strategy and roadmap development; governance and standards management; relevant cloud, application, integration, infrastructure, security, or data technologies; technology lifecycle planning; and risk and dependency management.

PREFERRED:

  • 10 to 12 years of experience
  • Advanced degree, MBA, or nationally recognized architecture, technology, or executive-level expertise
  • Relevant telecom industry or job-specific certifications.
  • TOGAF, FEAC, Open CA, CITA, SABSA, CCAr, cloud certifications (AWS, Azure, GCP), security certifications (CISSP, CISM), Agile / SAFe certifications, or practice-specific certifications, as applicable.

Work Requirements and Conditions:

  • Work is primarily sedentary, requiring daily routine computer usage.
  • Ability to work shifts assigned in a standard office/home-office setting and operate standard office equipment.
  • Ability to accurately communicate information and ideas and make valid judgments and decisions.
  • Available to work additional time on weekends, holidays, before or after normal work hours when necessary.
  • Must work well in a team environment and with a diverse group of people and customers.
  • Virtual workers must comply with remote-work policies and agreements.
  • The company operates in a 24/7 environment providing critical services and employees may be contacted outside core business hours to respond to emergencies.

Ensure productivity and discipline of site workforce.

Communicate clearly with management regarding site status and issues.

Proficient in reporting and documentation.

Site-based role, majority outdoor work environment.

title: Associate Director of Admissions & Athletics Liaison
description:
Earlham College is a Top 100 National Liberal Arts College located in Richmond, IN, a small city that's just a short drive away from several major metropolitan areas including Dayton, Cincinnati, Indianapolis and Chicago.

Richmond and Earlham have a symbiotic relationship. Through research, studies, internships and volunteering, Earlhamites offer Richmond expertise and service as Richmond offers our students the chance to gain valuable, real-world experience. Our community assumes no religious affiliation but follows Quaker principles and practices, which include respect for persons, integrity, a commitment to peace and justice, simplicity, and consensus-based community decision-making. Earlham is committed to and proud of being a diverse and inclusive place most clearly visible in our student body: 20% of our student body are international, coming from 60+ nations in 2022, and 24% are domestic students of color. Faculty and staff also bring tremendous diversity to the College; many have lived and worked outside the United States, and they make a point of drawing on those experiences in their interactions with students. Additionally, Earlham makes it a priority to serve as a safe and welcoming place for LGBTQ+ communities and has a four-star rating on the Campus Pride Index. Our community is characterized by respect for every person and a commitment to social justice. Equity and inclusion are central to Earlham's institutional priorities and our leadership is committed to widening the path to an Earlham education.

Position Overview

Reporting to the Associate Vice President for Enrollment, the Associate Director of Admissions is a member of Earlham College’s undergraduate admissions team responsible for managing an assigned domestic recruitment territory and serving as the primary Admissions liaison to the Athletics Department.

The Associate Director manages the recruitment and admissions process within their territory, building relationships with prospective students, families, school counselors, community organizations, and other partners. As Athletics liaison, the Associate Director works closely with coaches and Athletics staff to support the recruitment and enrollment of academically engaged student-athletes.

The Associate Director provides guidance to coaches, prospective student-athletes, and families on admissions requirements, timelines, academic expectations, financial aid, and enrollment processes; evaluates applications; monitors recruitment activity; and coordinates campus engagement opportunities. The position contributes as a member of the Admissions team but does not supervise admissions counselors or lead the College’s overall recruitment program.

Primary Duties & Responsibilities

Territory Management and Recruitment

  • Manage an assigned domestic recruitment territory and develop recruitment plans informed by enrollment goals, historical performance, market trends, and opportunities for growth.
  • Build and maintain relationships with prospective students, families, school counselors, community colleges, independent counselors, community organizations, and other key partners.
  • Manage prospective student relationships throughout the admissions funnel, from initial engagement through application, admission, yield, deposit, and enrollment.
  • Conduct high school visits, college fairs, counselor events, individual meetings, community programs, and other recruitment activities within the territory.
  • Monitor territory activity and funnel performance and adjust outreach strategies to support application, yield, deposit, and enrollment goals.
  • Maintain accurate and timely recruitment records in Slate and provide regular updates on territory activity, market conditions, opportunities, and challenges.
  • Represent Earlham at recruitment events and collaborate with Admissions leadership and Marketing and Communications on recruitment messaging and outreach.
  • Support on-campus and virtual admissions programs, including open houses, admitted student programs, counselor programs, and visit days.

Admissions and Athletics Partnership

  • Serve as the primary liaison between Admissions and Athletics for prospective student-athlete recruitment and enrollment.
  • For athletic programs operating below their optimal recruited student-athlete roster size, significantly increase applications (25%) from recruited student-athletes year over year, with the goal of driving measurable progress toward optimal roster size.
  • For athletics programs meeting or exceeding recruitment and roster goals, provide targeted strategies and support to help coaches successfully yield their top recruited student-athlete candidates.
  • Provide recruitment support for athletic programs that are reinstated or newly established by the College.
  • Evaluate prospective student athletes for the likely letter process.
  • Develop effective working relationships with coaches and Athletics staff and serve as a primary resource on admissions requirements, deadlines, academic expectations, financial aid, enrollment procedures, and relevant eligibility standards.
  • Coordinate recruitment activities for prospective student-athletes with coaches and Admissions leadership, ensuring alignment with Earlham’s enrollment priorities and NCAA Division III requirements.
  • Build relationships with prospective student-athletes and families and help them understand Earlham’s academic, residential, and athletic experiences.
  • Track prospective student-athletes from prospect through matriculation, maintain accurate records in Slate, and monitor recruitment activity, conversion, and enrollment outcomes.
  • Coordinate prospective student-athlete visits, interviews, open houses, recruiting events, and other campus engagement opportunities.
  • Recruit and train current student-athletes to participate appropriately in admissions tours, panels, presentations, and other prospective student engagement activities.
  • Provide training and guidance to coaches and Athletics staff on admissions processes, deadlines, recruitment practices, and the prospective student experience.
  • Collaborate with Athletics, Financial Aid, faculty, Student Life, and other campus partners to address recruitment and enrollment barriers and support a coordinated student experience.
  • Maintain familiarity with NCAA Division III regulations and Earlham policies relevant to student-athlete recruitment and refer compliance questions to appropriate institutional personnel.
  • Maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when handling student, admissions, financial, and athletics-related information.
  • Provide regular updates to Admissions and Athletics leadership regarding student-athlete recruitment activity, pipeline health, opportunities, and enrollment outcomes.

Admissions Evaluation and Enrollment

  • Participate in application review and admissions committee activities as assigned.
  • Evaluate applications, transcripts, recommendations, and other supporting materials in accordance with Earlham’s admissions policies and standards.
  • Conduct prospective student and applicant interviews, when applicable, and contribute thoughtful, holistic assessments of applicants.
  • Support admitted student yield efforts and communicate with students and families during key decision and enrollment periods.
  • Assist prospective student-athletes and their families in navigating admissions, financial aid, and enrollment requirements.
  • Assist with admissions events and programs, including planning, staffing, execution, and assessment.
  • Collaborate with Admissions colleagues on special projects, committees, communications, and recruitment initiatives.
  • Contribute to team training, professional development, and knowledge sharing as an experienced member of the Admissions staff, without formal supervisory responsibility.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Maintain current knowledge of Earlham’s academic programs, student experience, financial aid policies, admissions practices, Athletics programs, and enrollment priorities.
  • Represent Earlham through appropriate professional organizations, conferences, programs, and panels.
  • Ensure recruitment and admissions practices comply with institutional policies, NCAA Division III regulations, and applicable requirements.
  • Contribute to initiatives that advance equitable, inclusive, and diverse student recruitment and enrollment.
  • Participate in evening and weekend programs and travel during peak recruitment periods.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree preferred.
  • A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in college admissions, student recruitment, enrollment management, athletics administration, college advising, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated success in student recruitment, relationship management, and/or college counseling, with experience managing an admissions territory preferred.
  • Experience working with student-athletes, coaches, or collegiate athletics preferred.
  • Strong understanding of undergraduate admissions, the enrollment funnel, and NCAA Division III athletics; experience with non-scholarship student-athlete recruitment preferred.
  • Experience evaluating college applications, transcripts, and supporting materials preferred.
  • Experience with CRM systems and student information databases; Slate experience preferred. Familiarity with FrontRush or an athletics recruitment systems is a plus.
  • Excellent organizational, project-management, written, verbal, interpersonal, and presentation skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to build effective relationships with students, families, school counselors, coaches, and campus colleagues.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, recruitment activities, and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate across departments and manage complex recruitment pipelines.
  • Ability to exercise discretion and maintain confidentiality.
  • Commitment to equitable and diverse student recruitment and enrollment.
  • Appreciation for collaboration, consensus building, and the liberal arts.
  • Willingness to travel and work evenings and weekends during peak recruitment periods.

To Apply

Please submit the following materials with your application:

  • Cover letter
  • Resume
  • List of Three References with Contact Information

The review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.

Employee Benefits at Earlham

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance*
  • Company paid Long-Term Disability after 1 year of full-time service*
  • Basic and Voluntary Life insurance*
  • Employee Assistance Program*
  • Campus Store Discount
  • Free ticket vouchers for Richmond Symphony Orchestra
  • Wellness Center Free Membership or Discount for eligible employees
  • Athletic Games-Free entry to all home games
  • Free entry into most Theatre/Music shows
  • Tuition Benefits for Immediate Family for eligible employees*
  • 403(b) Retirement* – For eligible employees, Earlham will contribute a non-elective contribution equal to 5% of gross pay after 2 years of service. After 3 years of service, this non-elective contribution increases to 8%. Vesting credit is available for new employees with previous service in the education sector with required documentation.
  • Many Wayne County Chamber of Commerce member businesses offer discounts to anyone with an Earlham ID

*All employee benefit offerings are subject to employee eligibility per plan documents.

Earlham College is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination against any individual based on race, color, national origin, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, religion, or other protected classifications under applicable laws. The College is committed to building a diverse community that reflects the makeup of society and particularly welcomes and supports individuals from historically marginalized groups. As an institution with a Quaker identity, Earlham also encourages applications from members of the Religious Society of Friends (Quakers).

Earlham College complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and applicable state law. If you are an individual with a disability and require a reasonable accommodation to perform the essential functions of the position, or to participate in the hiring process, please contact the Earlham College Office of Human Resources.

title: Field Integrator/Technician
description:
The Systems Integrator (Installation/Service Technician position) is in the business of installing and servicing electronic security systems including, but not limited to, video surveillance systems, intrusion alarm systems, access control systems, gated entry systems, intercom systems, vehicle tracking systems, mobile video surveillance systems, A/V systems, Specialty Sensors and Devices, PA/Mass Notification Systems, solar system, etc. Most installs/service calls take place in the commercial environments that range from, but not limited to, SMB (small business) markets, Mulit-Family/HOA markets, agriculture/marina/industrial markets all the way to enterprise markets with a very small residential market of approximately 5%-10% of our book of business. Our organization is very proficient in retrofitting systems/integrations and most installations/service takes place while the business/community is operational thus a heavy emphasis on cleanliness and customer service is essential (some pre-construction jobs do occur). Most installations will require a large diversity of working environments and skills including, but not limited to, conduit running, concrete work (cutting, patching, slabs, pedestal/pole setting, etc), attic work, aerial runs, trenching (machine and hand digging), extension ladder/lift work, relay/timer/trigger programming, cloud portal management and programming, computer networking, etc. A keen construction understanding of building infrastructure is essential to understand where/how we can run wires, conduits, underground work, etc. Experience with and a strong understanding of heavy equipment, hand tools, ladders, etc. is required. Certain industry certification and product certifications are required or will be required to be obtained.


Work Schedule: Monday – Friday with occasional Saturdays. Hours vary based on client/company needs but generally have an 8AM start time and 5-6PM stop time; however, some later start times, delayed ending time and/or night work sometimes exist.


Travel Requirements: Our technicians travel throughout FL, GA & SC on a weekly basis. All drive/travel time is performed in company issued vehicles, compensated at full pay rate, covered with company expense accounts and per diem issued.


Experience Requirements: This role requires knowledge of analog and IP surveillance equipment, intrusion alarm systems, access control systems, gated entry systems, etc. including but not limited to; DVR’s, NVR’s, analog cameras, IP cameras, control panels, relays/timers/triggers, gate operators, intercoms, cloud connected devices, electronic locks/readers, enclosures, network racks, networking protocols, schemes, theories & devices, wireless communications and devices, low voltage wiring for VDV systems and applications as required by county and state codes, industry Best Practices running low voltage wiring, common safety procedures and knowledge of the use of hand and power tools associated with installation of such said systems.

*** Related industry experience can be considered such as: Cable/Internet/Satellite Technicians, Electricians, Fiber Optic Technicians, Telecom Technicians, Phone/Data/Network Cabling Technicians, etc.

Other Requirements: The individual will be required to furnish their own hand tools such as, but not limited to; screw drivers, scissors, wrenches, sheetrock saw, wire strippers, RJ45 crimpers, glow rods, sockets/ratchets, all forms of pliers/cutters, voltage meter, and any other hand tool needed to accomplish an install or service call. The individual will be required to lift heavy objects such as wire, ladders and other items, must have no felony or criminal record, pass drug screening and have a valid driver’s license with a clean driving record.

Training: This role has an on-boarding and training period of approximately 4-6(+/-) weeks as a ride along with a Trainer/Senior Technician. Based on experience some are 2 weeks and others are 6 weeks. While training you are still required to meet all stated qualifications.

Compensation: This role has a window of compensation that will range based on experience and skill-set. Rates are negotiable and based on those factors but generally range from $22.00/hr - $42.00/hr. These rates do not include per diem while traveling, commissions, etc. Rates/Offers will be discussed and agreed to at time of hire. We offer a full suite of benefits including, but not limited to, medical, dental, vision, life, 401K, etc.

title: Front-End Developer - Netflix Animation Studios
description:
Netflix Animation Studios is on a mission to entertain the world with bold, immersive animated films that are timeless and impactful. We are paving the way for the future of animation by building a community of amazing artists and talent across three vibrant locations globally. Come join us!

Do you have experience in software engineering and want to help shape the future of Netflix Animation Studios creating state-of-the-art tools?

The Production Tools Engineering team develops and supports technology used by the Production Management (Production) personnel at NAS. Our studio is distributed across three facilities: Vancouver, Burbank, and Sydney. The team develops and supports web applications and cloud-based tools built atop Netflix's world-class technology stack. Our team operates at the intersection of creativity, business, and technology at the studio with the goal of maximizing the operational efficiency of the Production team. We create, refine, and support state-of-the-art tools needed to fulfill the exciting slate of animated films being produced at NAS. We partner closely with other technology teams within both NAS and the Netflix corporation.

A team member in this role must be an experienced web front-end developer with strong UI/UX design sensibilities. The role requires someone capable of working in a modern tech stack using React, Vite, and Apollo Client for GraphQL. Important skills include root cause analysis, working effectively with service APIs, and an eye for good design. In addition, the role expects a developer who is comfortable interacting directly with Production users and requires someone with excellent interpersonal and communication skills. Experience working within the animation, VFX or games industries is highly preferred. Team members should be comfortable gathering user requirements, understanding use-cases, and providing white-glove support when necessary. This role offers freedom to learn and be technically creative while challenging you to collaborate on solutions to a wide variety of problems.

The complex, fast-paced environment demands team members with agility, curiosity, and alacrity. If this sounds like you, we’d love to talk.

What you’ll do:

  • Design, implement, and support web applications and UIs involving multiple features and external dependencies.
  • Implement and support integrations with Flow Production Tracking (aka ShotGrid) such as embedded web views and AMIs (action menu items).
  • Maintain and update existing web applications.
  • Partner with Production to understand workflows and translate them into technical solutions.

What You’ll Need:

  • Experience working in the animation, VFX, or games industries.
  • Experience with Flow Production Tracking.
  • 5+ years of experience as a front-end engineer.
  • Proficiency to write code in TypeScript. Experience with additional languages is highly preferred but not required.
  • Proficiency to read and comprehend code in multiple programming languages.
  • Experience with React, Vite, npm, and node.
  • A willingness to collaborate and compromise. The ideal candidate is an engineer and product owner - balancing their own vision with technical limitations, production needs, and contributions from colleagues.
  • You proactively identify opportunities to improve systems and workflows, not just implement tickets.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. You will represent the whole team in various meetings, gathering use cases, feedback, presenting solutions and more.
  • A strong background in computer science and a thorough understanding of software design patterns and best practices.
  • Experience collaborating with designers and translating designs into great user experiences.

Bonus:

  • Experience with other web frameworks, especially Vue.js.
  • Experience with Java and Python.
  • Experience with desktop UI frameworks such as PyQt.
  • Experience with service APIs using GraphQL and gRPC.

This role is based in Vancouver, British Columbia. Hybrid Role (Minimum of 3 days a week in the office).

At NAS, we carefully consider a wide range of compensation factors to determine your compensation. We rely on market indicators and consider your specific job family, background, location, skills, and experience. The overall market range for this role is typically $162,000 - $256,000 CAD. This reflects total compensation; we do not have stock options.

NAS benefits can include medical/dental/vision plans, mental health support, retirement programs, and family-forming benefits, paid leave of absence programs, and paid time away programs to be used for vacation and sick paid time off. See more detail about our benefits here.

Inclusion is a Netflix value and we strive to host a meaningful interview experience for all candidates. If you want an accommodation/adjustment for a disability or any other reason during the hiring process, please send a request to your recruiting partner.

We are an equal-opportunity employer and celebrate diversity, recognizing that diversity builds stronger teams. We approach diversity and inclusion seriously and thoughtfully. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, ancestry, national origin, caste, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic makeup, marital status, or military service.

title: Store Tech Solutions Architect
description:
The Store Tech Solutions Architect (Networking) is responsible for designing, implementing, and continuously enhancing the enterprise architecture that supports restaurant environments. This role leads the strategy, integration, and governance of networking, point‑of‑sale (POS), and security solutions across all locations, ensuring reliable, secure, and scalable infrastructure for both corporate and franchise operations.


The architect owns the end‑to‑end design of restaurant networking environments—including LAN/WAN, wireless, segmentation, and connectivity—to support POS systems, digital ordering platforms, kitchen technologies, and guest‑facing services. This role ensures high availability and performance of POS ecosystems, enabling seamless transactions and operational continuity across all brands.


The Solutions Architect collaborates closely with cross‑functional teams—including support organizations, system administrators, Category IT leaders, and retail project managers—to translate business and operational requirements into standardized, scalable technical solutions. The role also partners with firewall/security vendors, ISP providers, and POS technology partners to define architecture standards, drive vendor alignment, and ensure consistency across franchisee environments.


This position is accountable for embedding a robust, enterprise‑wide information security framework into all retail and restaurant technology designs. This includes proactively identifying, evaluating, and mitigating infrastructure and POS‑related security risks while ensuring compliance with regulatory standards and alignment with the company’s risk posture.


The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in networking, POS systems, and security architecture within retail or restaurant environments, along with strong knowledge of PCI DSS requirements and experience designing secure payment and transaction ecosystems.

title: HSE Specialist
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

This position’s overall mission is to help ensure occupational health and safety compliance, implement best practices, and continuously improve safety performance. Supporting operations in Knoxville, TN, this role works across departmental lines to support safe production processes and fosters a proactive safety culture throughout the facility.


RESPONSIBILITIES & DUTIES

  • Be present on the manufacturing floor, seek to understand operational challenges, and be a sought-after resource for risk mitigation and safety performance.
  • Ensure compliance with all applicable occupational safety and health regulations and Kelvion standards. Assist Operations in understanding, planning, and execution.
  • Coordinate safe work permit processes and job hazard analysis for high-risk activities (e.g., hot work, confined space entry), ensuring proper risk controls and approvals are in place.
  • Conduct regular safety audits, workplace inspections, and risk assessments to identify hazards and compliance gaps.
  • Collaborate with manufacturing, engineering, and maintenance teams to integrate safety controls into equipment and processes (e.g., machine guarding, ventilation systems) and ensure safe and ergonomic conditions.
  • Lead and/or support the implementation of safety improvement initiatives (e.g., engineering controls, procedural changes, or facility modifications) aimed at mitigating hazards and continuously enhancing safety performance.
  • Coordinate and ensure effective implementation of the safety function for key safety programs, such as PPE hazard assessments, chemical exposure sampling and mitigation, fire protection, lockout/tagout, machine guarding, and emergency preparedness and response.
  • Coordinate, develop and deliver effective safety training.
  • Lead or participate in incident investigations and facilitate root cause analysis.
  • Track, analyze, and report safety performance metrics for site and corporate management review, highlighting progress and areas for continuous improvement.
  • Maintain required safety documentation and records to ensure accurate, up-to-date compliance reporting and audit readiness.
  • Participate in broader continuous improvement initiatives with a safety focus, collaborating with colleagues and management to embed safety considerations into operational excellence efforts.
  • Contribute to building a safety-focused culture that empowers production teams to perform their work in a safe, compliant manner.
  • All other duties as assigned.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES

  • Working knowledge of occupational safety and health regulations and industry/engineering standards (e.g. ISO, ANSI, NFPA, ASME).
  • Strong technical, analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a fast-paced production environment.
  • Building positive relationships and influencing stakeholders.
  • Manufacturing process understanding.
  • Data analysis and reporting.
  • Continuous improvement mindset, with a demonstrated commitment to cultivating a positive safety culture across the organization.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE (required levels)

  • Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Health & Safety, or BS in other with ASP, CSP, or CHMM.
  • 2-5 years of experience in occupational health and safety (HSE) roles within a manufacturing environment (metal fabrication or heavy industry preferred).
  • Prefer Certified Safety Professional (CSP)
  • Prefer experience with safety management systems (e.g., ISO 45001)
  • Prefer Professional Engineer (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (FE) designation (Eng. Title).


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand; reach with hands, arms, and shoulders. SDET-I — Software Development Engineer in Test


We are looking for an SDET-I who is passionate about automation, quality engineering, and building scalable solutions that improve release confidence and engineering efficiency.

What You’ll Do

  • Build and maintain front-end automation for Android and iOS mobile applications, with a focus on reliable and scalable automation.
  • Understand critical user journeys and business workflows and identify the right scenarios to automate based on risk, impact and usage.
  • Take end-to-end ownership of automation — from identifying opportunities and designing solutions to implementation, execution, debugging and continuous improvement.
  • Drive automation initiatives proactively and continuously identify gaps in automation coverage and quality.
  • Integrate automation into CI/CD pipelines to provide fast and actionable feedback during development and releases.
  • Focus on outcomes, not test-case count — improve regression time, automation reliability, defect detection and release confidence.
  • Use AI/GenAI tools and approaches to accelerate test-case generation, automation development, test maintenance, failure analysis and identify new automation opportunities.
  • Collaborate with Developers, Product and QA teams to build testable, high-quality products.
  • Investigate automation failures, perform root-cause analysis and ensure issues are driven to closure.

What We’re Looking For

  • 2–4 years of experience in SDET / QA Automation / Software Testing.
  • Hands-on experience with mobile automation using Appium, MCP, Flutter testing frameworks or equivalent.
  • Strong programming skills in Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Dart or similar.
  • Good understanding of UI, API and end-to-end testing.
  • Experience with CI/CD, Git and automation frameworks.
  • Experience using AI/GenAI for test automation or software testing is highly desirable.
  • Strong problem-solving, debugging and analytical skills.
  • A quality and outcome-oriented mindset with a strong sense of ownership.

Success in This Role


Identify what matters → Automate what matters → Own the automation → Measure the outcome → Continuously improve.


Life at PeepalCo


We take great pride in what we do and are committed to our mission. And we have a lot of fun while at it!

  • Customer-first: That’s the North Star. Everything we do is to make our users’ investment experience better and simplified.

  • Data-driven: The source of truth. Simple as that.

title: Senior Python Data Scraping Engineer (Freelance)
description:
Mindrift is looking for highly skilled Vibecode specialists to join the Tendem project () and drive specialized data scraping workflows for real-world use cases. Mindrift is looking for highly skilled Senior Python Data Scraping Engineers to join the Tendem project and drive specialized data scraping workflows for real-world applications. In this role, you'll apply your expertise in web scraping, data extraction, and data processing to deliver accurate, reliable, and high-quality results. This part-time remote opportunity is ideal for technical professionals with hands-on experience in web scraping, data extraction and processing.

What We Do

The Mindrift platform connects specialists with innovative technology projects. Our mission is to help develop high-quality AI technologies by combining real-world expertise from professionals across the globe with advanced AI development efforts.

About the Role

This is a freelance role for a Tendem project. As a Senior Python Data Scraping Engineer, you'll handle data scraping tasks requiring technical precision for web extraction and processing, utilizing tools such as Apify, OpenRouter, and other technologies, alongside your own technical expertise and approaches.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end data extraction workflows across complex websites, ensuring complete coverage, accuracy, and reliable delivery of structured datasets.
  • Leverage available tools and custom workflows to accelerate data collection, validation, and task execution while meeting defined requirement.
  • Ensure reliable extraction from dynamic and interactive web sources, adapting approaches as needed to handle JavaScript-rendered content and changing site behavior.
  • Enforce data quality standards through validation checks, cross-source consistency controls, adherence to formatting specifications, and systematic verification prior to delivery.
  • Scale scraping operations for large datasets using efficient batching or parallelization, monitor failures, and maintain stability against minor site structure changes.

Educational qualifications

  • At least 5+ years of relevant experience in data engineering, web scraping, automation, or software development (required).
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, or related technical fields is a plus.

Academic and/or Professional Experience

Candidates should have a strong technical foundation and practical experience with scripting, automation, and data extraction workflows. title: Test Technician I
description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies’ core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

This role is part of our Hypersonics and Strategic Missile Defense business, which designs, develops, and delivers highly dependable missile systems for hypersonic and strategic missile defense missions. We provide integrated, mission-ready hardware that brings together multiple technologies into unified systems engineered to perform in demanding operational environments. Our tip-to-tail capabilities include payload protection and deployment systems, propulsion systems, aerodynamic interstage systems, separation systems, missile subsystems, shroud systems, launch systems, and payload integration solutions.

In this role, you help ensure mission-critical hardware performs reliably by executing tests that simulate extreme environmental and operational conditions. Working closely with engineers and senior technicians, you support test setup, execution, data collection, and documentation across component, subsystem, and system-level testing. You also assist with environmental testing and lab maintenance while operating independently in a fast-paced test environment.

Responsibilities

  • Supports test planning and execution, including test design, analysis, procedure writing, and data collection.
  • Performs setup and teardown of fixturing, equipment, and instrumentation according to engineering procedures.
  • Applies knowledge of military and commercial testing specifications.
  • Performs lab maintenance and process improvements.
  • Communicates effectively and collaborates well with team members.
  • Works independently with limited supervision.

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or General Educational Development (GED).
  • One to two years of experience in aerospace, defense, or manufacturing environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to work in a test environment through prior work experience.
  • Ability and willingness to obtain a Washington State explosives license and work with energetic devices.
  • Proficiency with computers and familiarity with common office applications.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate’s degree or higher.

Physical Requirements

  • Uses stairs regularly.

This position requires U.S. person status under U.S. export control laws, including U.S. citizens and nationals, lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees.

title: Catalyse Founders: Seeking Ambitious Recruitment Head Hunters To Head Their Own Desk — Hong Kong & Singapore Location: Hong Kong & Singapore Employment Type: Full-Time

description:

Job Title: Founding Partners — Hong Kong & Singapore
Location: Hong Kong & Singapore
Employment Type: Full-Time Business Partnership

Catalyse Founders: Seeking Ambitious Recruitment Head Hunters To Head Their Own Desk — Hong Kong & Singapore Location: Hong Kong & Singapore Employment Type: Full-Time

An invitation to ambitious recruitment professionals ready to take control of their own desk.

In large recruitment agencies, training often stops the moment you start billing. You are left to figure out the next steps on your own, pressured by monthly KPIs to push volume over quality. And what fills the vacuum where real mentorship should be? Office gossip. Corridor politics. A culture where people talk about each other instead of developing each other. Where your reputation is shaped not by your results, but by who you sit next to and whose favour you carry. It is exhausting, and it is holding you back.

The Catalyse Founders Group is a boutique recruitment practice that rejects both the volume-driven factory model and the toxic culture that sustains it. We are seeking ambitious head hunters in Hong Kong and Singapore who want the autonomy to head their own desk, backed by the infrastructure and genuine mentorship of an established institutional group.

The Path to Mastery We are looking for professionals with proven recruitment experience who are ready for honest self-reflection. You know how to recruit, but you want to learn how to build a business.

To get there, you must confront what we call the Natural Limit — the internal patterns that hold capable recruiters back. The gossip culture of large firms does not just waste your time; it actively deepens these patterns. It amplifies your insecurity through constant comparison, rewards people-pleasing over honest client qualification, and substitutes the appearance of busyness for genuine strategic work.

Through our Eternal Question coaching framework, we work with you directly to identify and overcome these constraints. We will help you eliminate the fear that causes hesitation, the need to accommodate low-yield clients and internal politics, the illusion of busyness, and the misapplication of your energy. We do not just want you to bill more; we want to develop your executionary power so you can operate like a principal.

The Opportunity You will be given the mandate to head your own desk within a culture built on candour, accountability, and mutual respect — the opposite of what you have experienced. While this role begins with heading a desk, exceptional performers who embrace our methodology will be evaluated for our Founding Partner co-ownership model.

Candidate Profile

• Solid recruitment experience in Hong Kong or Singaporewith verifiable billing success.

• A strong desire to transition from executing tasks toleading a market segment.

• A commitment to continuous learning and an openness toour coaching methodology.

• The discipline to abandon comfortable habits in favourof structured, high-yield execution.

How to Apply

Please submit your CV and a concise, confidential covering letter to

inquiries@firstcapital.asia

addressing two points:

1.Why heading your own desk within a boutique framework represents the right next step for you, rather than conventional agency progression.

2.Which of the four Natural Limit patterns (fear/hesitation, compulsion to please, busyness without productivity, or unfocused energy) most closely describes a constraint you have personally experienced, and how you have attempted to address it.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. We look forward to a candid conversation.

The instructor would also coordinate the MEI Apprenticeship Training Program and oversee training initiatives associated with the same as well as initiatives involving team member mentorship, field coaches, on-the-job training (OJT), Best Known Methods (BKMs), and employment candidate evaluations / interviewing. Will also assist with identifying employee and staff training requirements and development needs.

  • Perform gap analyses and evaluate employee proficiencies to aid in determining appropriate development paths.

They transform complex financial data into clear, actionable business insights, manage enterprise financial performance, and lead an internal team of financial analysts. A successful candidate will have a blend of financial strategy, strong knowledge of financial controls and regulation along with exceptional leadership skills.


Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Develop trusted partnerships with executive and operational leadership to understand business drivers and provide financial insights that support decision making.
  • Lead an annual budget, multi-year financial plan, rolling forecasts and ongoing performance across the organization.
  • Analyze trends in revenue, gross margin, labor, overhead, and other key operating metrics for financial optimization.
  • Provide actionable insights into profitability, capital planning and operational performance.
  • Exceptional communication, stakeholder management, and the ability to explain complex financial concepts to non-financial leaders.
  • Monitor and drive the analysis of key performance indicators and communicate emerging trends, risks, and opportunities to operational leadership, and provide recommendations to executive leadership to drive performance enhancements.
  • Oversee capital expenditure reporting, tracking, budgeting, and investment analyses
  • Prepare, examine, and analyze financial records, systems, and activities for efficiencies and opportunities.
  • Oversee the design and maintenance of monthly financial reporting packages, variance analyses, and performance dashboards.
  • Develop and maintain financial models used for budgeting, forecasting, pricing analyses, and business planning.
  • Collaborate with Accounting to improve data integrity, reporting accuracy, and financial processes.
  • Collaborate with Regional Vice Presidents and Operations Leadership to provide analytical support for offices and regions to improve decision making and visibility.
  • Support strategic initiatives, acquisitions, and other special projects through financial analysis as assigned.
  • Lead, drive, and ensure consistency between regions for budgeting process or companywide established processes.
  • Serve as a strategic leader responsible for setting the organization’s direction, aligning teams with mission-critical goals, and fostering a culture of innovation and accountability. Build strong cross-functional relationships to influence decision-making and drive performance.
  • Partner with the CFO to design, build and develop a high-performing FP&A team, including organizational design, talent improvement, processes, and operating cadence.
  • Support and review existing processes, creating new processes to drive national operational support.
  • Perform other duties as necessary and requested.


Minimum Qualifications (Experience, Skills, and Education):

  • MBA in finance required or a Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business, or related field combined with work experience to demonstrate mastery of field.
  • 7 – 10+ years of experience in financial planning and analysis, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.
  • 5+ years in a direct management or leadership capacity.
  • Knowledge of US GAAP and thorough understanding of all financial statements.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify trends, investigate variances, and recommend practical business improvements to business leaders.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills; ability to communicate financial information to both finance and non-finance stakeholders.
  • Ability to develop and maintain strong working relationships with cross-functioning teams.
  • Ability to work independently and prioritize tasks in a fast-paced environment.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills (PivotTables, XLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH, Power Query or similar, complex formulas, financial modeling).
  • Experience developing reports and dashboards using Power BI or similar business intelligence tools preferred.
  • Experience with Microsoft D365 or a similar ERP system preferred.
  • Able to travel as needed.


Physical Requirements and Working Conditions:

Normal temperature-controlled office environment. Will frequently use a computer, keyboard / mouse, cellular or office telephone, and regular business office equipment. Extended periods of sitting for long durations, occasional walking, and lifting up to ten pounds. Occasional walking over uneven outdoor terrain and/or exposure to inclement weather, non-temperature-controlled environments, or warehouse-type environments.


Additional Requirements:

Must be able to work in a high functioning team environment. Display the highest levels of honesty, integrity, and professionalism. Take pride in your work and in the company. Communicate openly and strive for peak performance in daily tasks. Know and deliver the quality service MEI’s customers have come to expect.

Sanneh Foundation Mission

The mission of Sanneh is to empower youth, improve lives, and unite communities. Position Description

The Workforce Program Capacity Building VISTA will support the development and implementation of workforce readiness programs designed to provide career development and employment opportunities for youth, especially those from diverse and low-income backgrounds. This position will be based at Conway and will focus on building sustainable partnerships with local businesses, organizations, and stakeholders to enhance job training, internship, and employment opportunities for participants in Sanneh programs. The VISTA will also work to streamline internal processes, improve program efficiency, and increase overall impact.


Role and Responsibilities

Build partnerships with local businesses, organizations, and stakeholders to expand workforce development opportunities for youth. Strengthen the internal systems and processes for tracking, reporting, and improving the impact of workforce readiness programs. Empower youth with the skills, confidence, and resources needed to secure employment and succeed in their careers.

ACTIVITIES (Q1-4):

  • Orientation and Program Familiarization

    • Learn the history and goals of Sanneh’s workforce readiness programs, and become familiar with current initiatives and the needs of youth participants.

    • Understand existing processes for job training, internships, and employer partnerships.

  • Partnership Development and Outreach

    • Assist in building and maintaining sustainable partnerships with local businesses, schools, community organizations, and other stakeholders to expand job training and internship opportunities for youth.

    • Engage in outreach efforts to identify new employer partners and job opportunities, increasing the number of available internships and employment placements.

  • Job Readiness Workshop Design

    • Collaborate with staff to design and coordinate job readiness workshops that provide youth with essential career skills, including resume writing, interview techniques, and workplace etiquette.

    • Facilitate or support job readiness sessions to ensure that participants gain practical, hands-on experience and knowledge.

ACTIVITIES (Q1-4):

    • Assist in tracking the progress of program participants, ensuring that they meet their employment and training goals.

    • Collect feedback from youth participants to evaluate the effectiveness of the workforce readiness programs and identify areas for improvement.

  • Internal Systems and Process Improvement

    • Support the development of efficient internal systems for data collection and reporting on program outcomes.

    • Streamline communication strategies to improve outreach to youth participants and ensure that all stakeholders are informed and engaged in workforce readiness efforts.

ACTIVITIES (Q1-4):

    • Support efforts to connect youth participants with potential employers, including job fairs, networking events, and other opportunities for direct employer engagement.

    • Monitor the success of job placements and internships, and work with employers to ensure ongoing opportunities for youth in Sanneh programs.

  • Documentation and Reporting

    • Assist with documenting program outcomes, success stories, and areas for growth in workforce development efforts.

    • Contribute to the creation of reports or presentations that showcase the impact of workforce readiness programs for funders and other stakeholders.

ACTIVITIES (Q1-4):

  • Capacity Building and Sustainability

    • Collaborate with staff to ensure the long-term sustainability of the workforce development programs, including establishing procedures and resources that can be maintained after the VISTA term.

    • Develop materials and resources that support program expansion and provide tools for ongoing success in workforce readiness efforts.

title: Entry Level- Test Engineer (Onsite- Aberdeen Maryland)
description:
ENTRY-LEVEL TEST ENGINEER

xG and Mixed Signal Product Development | Technical Services

About the opportunity

Fairwinds Technologies is continuously looking for curious, methodical, and hands-on early-career engineers who want to verify that advanced communications, RF, embedded-computing, and mixed-signal products perform as intended. In this role, you may support either our xG or Mixed Signal product development team, or technical-services contracts aligned with those product areas.

You will work alongside experienced test, systems, RF, network, DSP, FPGA, embedded software, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, and quality personnel to plan tests, configure equipment, collect evidence, analyze results, troubleshoot failures, and improve repeatability. Assignments may span internal product development and customer-funded research, integration, qualification, demonstration, acceptance, and field-support activities.

What you will do

  • Help translate product, system, interface, and customer requirements into clear test objectives, methods, procedures, data needs, and acceptance criteria.
  • Develop and maintain test plans, test cases, procedures, checklists, test configurations, data sheets, traceability records, and formal test reports.
  • Configure and operate laboratory equipment, radios, network devices, embedded systems, channel emulators, RF components, computers, and automated test environments.
  • Execute functional, performance, interoperability, regression, environmental-support, reliability, and acceptance testing under established procedures.
  • Collect, organize, visualize, and analyze test data for metrics such as signal quality, frequency response, gain, noise, throughput, latency, packet loss, error rate, timing, thermal behavior, and system stability.
  • Use oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, network analyzers, power meters, logic analyzers, packet-capture tools, and comparable instruments as appropriate to the assignment.
  • Create Python, MATLAB, Bash, or other scripts to automate equipment control, configuration checks, data collection, analysis, plotting, and report inputs.
  • Document test anomalies, reproduce failures, isolate contributing conditions, support root-cause investigations, and verify corrective actions.
  • Coordinate test readiness, equipment availability, calibration status, software and firmware baselines, test articles, interfaces, safety controls, and configuration records.
  • Participate in laboratory and field testing, customer demonstrations, design reviews, test-readiness reviews, and technical-service deliverables.

Technology and mission areas

Depending on assignment, you may contribute in one or more of the following areas:

  • xG wireless systems, including 5G, non-terrestrial networking, tactical communications, software-defined radio, mesh and mobile networks, radio integration, gateways, and edge-compute platforms.
  • Mixed Signal products, including Global Link and EchoPhase-related capabilities, channel emulation, coherent combining, wideband RF systems, high-speed digital and data-converter interfaces, and embedded control.
  • Radio and network performance, interoperability, RF translation, signal-path alignment, waveform behavior, channel effects, synchronization, calibration, and system management.
  • Integrated systems that combine RF, antennas, DSP, FPGA logic, embedded Linux, networking, power, mechanical packaging, firmware, and management software.
  • Government-funded R&D and technical-services contracts involving test planning, configuration, integration, performance characterization, documentation, demonstrations, acceptance support, and field troubleshooting.

Minimum qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Engineering Technology, or a closely related technical field, completed or expected before start date.
  • Coursework, laboratory, internship, capstone, research, maker-space, or personal-project experience involving test, measurement, troubleshooting, integration, data analysis, or technical documentation.
  • Foundational understanding of the engineering test lifecycle, including objectives, configurations, procedures, measurement, repeatability, acceptance criteria, and reporting.
  • Basic experience using laboratory instruments, software tools, command-line utilities, or data-analysis applications to investigate technical behavior.
  • Ability to follow controlled procedures while recognizing unexpected results, asking good questions, and documenting observations accurately.
  • Ability to use structured problem solving, organize test evidence, communicate assumptions, and explain results clearly.
  • Ability to collaborate in a multidisciplinary engineering environment and satisfy customer, site-access, export-control, and security requirements associated with assigned work.

Preferred, not required

  • Hands-on experience testing radios, networks, electronics, embedded systems, RF components, software, mechanical hardware, or integrated prototypes.
  • Exposure to Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, Bash, Linux, Git, instrument-control interfaces, automated test frameworks, or continuous integration.
  • Familiarity with RF or electronic test equipment, packet analysis, traffic generation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, or environmental test equipment.
  • Coursework or project experience in wireless communications, RF systems, digital signal processing, 5G or LTE, non-terrestrial networks, software-defined radio, satellite communications, computer networks, or embedded systems.
  • Awareness of requirements traceability, verification matrices, regression testing, configuration management, calibration, uncertainty, statistical analysis, or quality systems.
  • Experience preparing technical plots, concise findings, test reports, troubleshooting logs, or customer-facing engineering documentation.

What success looks like

  • First 90 days: learn the assigned product or program, laboratory environment, test equipment, safety practices, configuration workflow, requirements, and acceptance criteria; execute scoped tests with mentoring.

  • Work on products and customer-funded R&D activities within the same technical domain, connecting requirements and engineering designs with measured performance and operational use cases.

  • Learn from experienced multidisciplinary personnel while receiving meaningful test-planning, equipment, automation, troubleshooting, analysis, and documentation responsibilities early in your career.
  • Join a growing technology organization expanding its xG and Mixed Signal portfolios and strengthening repeatable product-development, verification, and technical-service practices.

How to apply

Submit your resume and, if available, links or short descriptions for relevant test plans, laboratory work, automation scripts, data analyses, capstone projects, research, internships, troubleshooting activities, technical papers, or portfolios. Tell us what you tested, what you personally contributed, how you controlled the test and evaluated the result, and what you learned.

description:
KI VAGY TE

Egy együttműködő, megbízható és vásárló-orientált személy vagy.
Képes vagy saját munkádat megszervezni és feladataidat priorizálni a hatékony időkihasználás érdekében.
Vállalod a több műszakos (délelőtti, délutáni, esti és hétvégi) munkavégzést.
Jó állóképességgel rendelkezel, rugalmasan állsz a munkához, és tudod vállalni a nehéz fizikai munka (30 kg-nál nehezebb termékek emelése).
Remek csapatjátékos vagy, ugyanakkor önállóan is tudsz dolgozni.
Felhasználói szintű számítógépes ismerettel rendelkezel.
Elmúltál 18 éves.
A logisztikai tapasztalat előnyt jelent, de motivált pályakezdők jelentkezését is szívesen fogadjuk.

EGY NAP VELÜNK

A vásárlói rendeléseket pontosan, időben, sérülésmentesen és a biztonsági előírások betartásával összekészíted a vásárló számára.
A termékeket a piactérről és a raktárból összegyűjtöd, ellenőrződ vagy csomagolod.
A termékek összegyűjtése során akár 10-15 km-t is gyalogolsz egy műszakon belül.
A munkakör 8 órás munkaszerződés keretében, 10 órás műszakokban történő munkavégzést jelent.

EGYÜTT CSAPATKÉNT

Az IKEA áruházakban sok mindennel foglalkozunk. De egy dolog közös – emberekkel és lakberendezéssel dolgozunk. Célunk, hogy jobb hétköznapokat teremtsünk az emberek többsége számára. Ezt nap mint nap tesszük, amikor találkozunk vásárlóinkkal.



A kiválasztási folyamatban elég, ha csatolod az önéletrajzodat, - a motivációs levéltől eltekintünk - és az online jelentkezés során megválaszolsz néhány egyszerű kérdést.
Miután elküldted a jelentkezésed, átnézzük a pályázatokat, és ha megfelelsz a feltételeknek, meghívunk egy interjúra.
A kommunikáció főként e-mailben zajlik, ezért figyeld a beérkező leveleket (és a spam mappát is).
Köszönjük, hogy érdeklődsz – várjuk, hogy megismerhessünk!

AMIT KÍNÁLUNK

Stabil munkahely vagyunk, legális munkáltatói háttérrel, hosszútávú munkalehetőséggel.
Saját szervezésű programjaink mellett képzésekkel, karrierlehetőséggel és baráti legkörrel várunk, ahol tényleg fontos vagy te és a csapat is.
Igényes munkakörülmények között töltheted el a munkaidődet és szüneteidet, egy hónapra előre kiadott munkaidőbeosztással.
Államilag elrendelt ünnepnapokon zárva tartunk és ezen felül december 24-én, illetve december 31-én is, mely napokat az IKEA szabadnapként biztosítja.

JUTTATÁSI CSOMAG:
Éves Cafeteria keret
15% személyzeti kedvezmény az IKEA áruházakban történő vásárláshoz
Önkéntes Nyugdíjpénztári vagy Egészségpénztári hozzájárulás
Személyzeti étterem és további étkezési hozzájárulás havonta
Dolgozói támogató programok (jogi, egészségügyi, pénzügyi, életvezetési tanácsadás)
Munkatársi bónusz program
Legalább 25 nap szabadság minden munkatársának (az alap- és életkor után járó pótszabadsággal együtt)

Csatlakozz hozzánk, és egy olyan cég része lehetsz, ahol önmagadért értékelnek. Mindannyian egy nagy, befogadó csapatot alkotunk, és azért dolgozunk, hogy emberek millióinak életére legyünk pozitív hatással.

JOB TITLE: Overnight Parking Lot Sweeper– Full-Time
LOCATION: Virginia Beach, VA.

TRAVEL: None (0%)​

Who we are:
Sweeping Corporation of America (SCA) is the nation’s leading street sweeping company, operating in over 20 states and supporting more than 600 municipalities, counties, and government agencies. With over six million miles serviced annually, SCA is uniquely focused on the delivery of high-performance street sweeping, jet-vac, and environmental services. SCA has built its entire organization, its people, processes, technology, and investments around providing uninterrupted, accountable, and results-driven services tailored to the needs of our clients. Our mission is to provide essential sweeping and environmental services that support cleaner, safer, and more sustainable communities.

Your daily impact:
As our next Parking Lot Sweeper, you'll be at the heart of our mission—delivering essential services that help improve public safety and enhance environmental quality. You’ll take ownership of assigned routes including shopping centers and parking lots, drive the parking lot sweeper, and operate specialized equipment to ensure parking areas are clean and well-maintained.
The job responsibilities below outline the core duties and expectations of this position, providing clarity on how the role supports Company goals. However, not all duties can be listed, and as business needs evolve, responsibilities may shift over time to reflect new priorities, processes, or technologies:

Safety & Inspection: Perform required pre-trip and post-trip inspections of equipment in accordance with company standards. Ensure all safety features are operational before beginning route.

Execution: Review assigned routes thoroughly prior to departure. Be proactive in asking clarifying questions if the route or expectations are unclear. Complete assigned jobs within the allotted timeframe while maintaining expected quality and attention to detail.

Equipment Operation: Operate equipment safely and efficiently at all times, following all traffic laws, company safety procedures, and site-specific protocols. Exercise additional caution during inclement weather or challenging site conditions.

Material Handling: Handle materials safely and securely; Apply correct procedures for material types and disposal sites.

Reporting: Report any equipment issues, malfunctions, near misses, crashes, or injuries within 30 minutes or as soon as safely possible. Immediately escalate opportunities, work issues, or safety concerns to management.

Professional Communication: Maintain a professional attitude and appearance while representing the company on job sites or in public areas. Communicate effectively with team members, supervisors, and clients when needed.

Compliance & Documentation: Accurately complete required logs, manifests, and forms.

Adaptability & Problem Solving: Respond appropriately to changes and challenges; identify and solve issues timely.

Regular & Predictable Attendance: The ability to consistently report to work on time and as scheduled, with minimal unexcused absences. This includes being present and prepared to work throughout assigned shifts, and reliably adhering to start times, breaks, and end times.

Minimum Job Requirements:
Minimum job qualifications define the essential skills, experience, and abilities needed to succeed in the role. They set the baseline for hiring but may evolve as the job and business requirements change:

Education: ​High School or GED​

Experience: 1 year driving experience preferred

License: Driver’s License

Age: Must be at least 21 years of age

Compliance: Must maintain an acceptable driving record and successfully pass a motor vehicle record (MVR) check, background check, DOT physical, and drug screening in accordance with Company policy and applicable law.

Skills & Competencies:
Skills and competencies define the abilities and behaviors essential for success in the role. They guide performance expectations and may evolve as the role, team, or business priorities change:

Safety & Compliance Focus: Ability to follow safety procedures, conduct inspections, operate equipment responsibly, and comply with all traffic, site, and regulatory requirements.

Operational Execution & Reliability: Strong ability to plan routes, complete work efficiently and accurately, adapt to changing conditions, and maintain consistent, dependable attendance.

Communication & Issue Reporting: Effectively communicate with supervisors and teammates, represent the Company professionally, and promptly report equipment issues, incidents, or safety concerns.

Physical Requirements:
Physical requirements outline the essential on-the-job demands needed to perform the role safely and effectively.

Work Environment & Exposure: Constant work outdoors with regular exposure to weather, elements, and traffic; occasional exposure to loud noise, dust/debris, and jarring conditions; limited exposure to chemicals.

Physical Demands: Frequent sitting and walking/standing; occasional bending, twisting, squatting, kneeling, pushing/pulling; limited stair climbing and crawling; ability to lift and carry up to 75lbs at varying heights, including overhead.

Cognitive & Sensory Requirements: Continuous reading, screen use, mental focus, and hand-eye coordination throughout the workday.

Safety is #1:
Our safety culture is more than a policy—it’s a mindset. We have a full-time safety team, rigorous training programs, and detailed operating procedures to protect our people and the communities we serve. You’ll be supported from Day One with the tools and knowledge to work confidently and safely.

Benefits & Wellness at SCA:
We believe great people deserve great perks. When you join SCA, you’re not just keeping the streets clean—you’re paving the way to a better future (with some solid benefits under the hood).
Here’s what we’ve got in our hopper:

401(k) with Match: Plan for the long haul—retirement is another kind of clean sweep.

Weekly Pay: Consistent weekly pay you can count on, plus on-demand pay so you can access earned wages when you need them.

Health, Dental, Vision & Life Insurance: Take care of what matters most with benefits designed to support you and your family’s wellbeing and future.

Short- & Long-Term Disability: If life throws a pothole your way, we help you keep rolling.

Indemnity Insurance: Extra protection for life’s unexpected detours.

Paid Time Off & Holidays: Even the best machines need downtime.

Training Programs: Shift into high gear with learning and career advancement opportunities.

Team Focus: We show up for our customers and each other, every day.

A Culture that Cares: People are the heart of everything we do, fostering a culture of respect, safety, and growth
Rooted in Respect: A company with a name people know & trust - built on relationships, community pride and a people focused approach to leadership.

Ready to sweep your career to the next level? Apply today and join the SCA team!
