title: Director of Sustainable Investing
description:
Empowering Financial Futures.

For more than 65 years, Glenmede’s independent ownership, innovation and unwavering commitment to our clients have made us a trusted partner for private wealth, endowment & foundation, and investment management clients.

Our people are invaluable. Through a team-oriented environment, your knowledge, expertise and varied backgrounds contribute to thoughtful innovation. Our culture fosters opportunities for continuous career growth and development in all areas of the organization. Working at Glenmede, you will experience the infrastructure and resources of a large firm combined with the client and employee focus of an independently owned boutique.

This position will operate in a hybrid work environment, 3 days per week in the office (Philadelphia, PA).

OVERVIEW:

The Director of Sustainable Investing will lead Glenmede’s Sustainable Investing group, a firmwide capability within Investment Strategy & Research that serves private wealth, endowment & foundation, and institutional clients. This role advances the platform’s growth, visibility, and client impact by bringing together sustainable investing expertise, client engagement, thought leadership, and business development support.

Glenmede has built a differentiated and established sustainable investing capability. The next phase of its development will emphasize enhancing business alignment: strengthening the connection between investment offerings, client implementation, thought leadership, and business priorities. The successful candidate will be a commercially oriented platform leader and sustainable investing subject-matter specialist, with the investment fluency needed to partner effectively with Manager Research and business-line investment teams.

This individual will work closely with investment and client-facing professionals across all functions and departments, including manager research, portfolio management, relationship management, business development, marketing and legal. Additionally, this individual will develop and maintain industry relationships and will represent Glenmede internally and externally.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Sustainable Investing Framework and Expertise

  • Contribute the sustainable investing perspective to Glenmede’s investment platform, helping develop and refine the frameworks used to assess mission and values alignment and inform strategy evaluation and appropriate client utilization.
  • Partner with the Manager Research Group, and where appropriate business-line investment teams, contributing a sustainable investing perspective on strategies under evaluation for the platform.
  • Help establish and maintain clear definitions, decision frameworks, documentation standards, and governance, including the discipline around intended versus unintended deviation and return concession.
  • Ensure the platform is implementable and scalable, with appropriate escalation paths between relationship and portfolio management teams and the Sustainable Investing group.

Client Relationship Support

  • Serve as a senior subject-matter expert in client and prospect meetings, particularly for complex, highly engaged, and mission-focused relationships.
  • Support relationship managers and portfolio managers in translating client mission, values, and investment objectives into portfolios.

Business Development and Growth

  • Source opportunities through industry presence, centers of influence, and allocator-level conference access.
  • Hand off opportunities to Business Development for qualification, development, and conversion, and re-engage selectively where differentiated expertise supports closing.
  • Define and measure the platform’s contribution to the business using balanced metrics that distinguish sourcing, influence, development, and closing.

Thought Leadership and External Representation

  • Advance Glenmede’s external presence and market perspective through thought leadership on sustainable and mission-aligned investing.
  • Connect published perspectives explicitly to capabilities Glenmede can deliver.
  • Represent the firm at conferences, with industry organizations, and in other external forums.

Institutional Stewardship

  • Lead and develop the Sustainable Investing team, fostering collaboration, accountability, and continued professional growth.
  • Steward established institutional infrastructure, including the Sustainable Advisory Council, the internal Guiding Coalition, and the Best Practices program, and extract increasing practical value from each.
  • Develop training, tools, and resources that help relationship and portfolio managers communicate sustainable investing capabilities with confidence.

Firm Building

  • Active engagement in department-specific and firm-wide initiatives to expand capabilities, create solutions to unmet business needs, improve client experience, or develop more efficient processes.
  • Contribute to the advancement of team, office, and business capabilities.
  • Participate in ad hoc projects requested by management.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree.
  • 10+ years of experience in investment management, wealth management, or a related field, including meaningful experience in sustainable, mission-aligned, or impact investing.
  • Demonstrated experience leading a platform, program, or investment capability across multiple stakeholders or business lines.
  • Experience in client-facing or advisory settings with sophisticated individual or institutional clients.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

title: Technical Delivery Manager
description:
About Progress Partners

Progress Partners is a fast-growing technology company building and scaling next-generation SaaS and mobile platforms. We blend creativity with data-driven execution to ship high-impact products, including AI-powered tools, productivity platforms, and workflow software, used by millions of people in more than 160 countries.

Our global team of experts in software development, product design, growth, and analytics collaborates across time zones to deliver category-defining innovations. We work end-to-end across the product lifecycle: design, build, launch, and scale.

If you’re passionate about building transformative products, Progress Partners is a place to make a lasting impact.

About the Role

We're looking for an Engineering Delivery Manager to strengthen delivery predictability, quality, and visibility across our external engineering teams.

This is a strategic, company-side engineering delivery role, not a traditional line-management role. You won't manage engineers directly. Instead, you'll work with lead-level stakeholders across several teams to understand how work is planned and delivered, surface risks and bottlenecks early, and drive measurable improvement. You'll work closely with external engineering and vendor leads, product managers, engineering and technical leads, QA, platform engineering, and business stakeholders.

What You’ll Do

  • Build clear visibility into what each external team is working on, who owns what, and where delivery risk sits.

  • Ensure delivery plans are realistic, transparent, and tied to business priorities — and track progress against them.

  • Spot teams falling behind early, not after deadlines slip, and diagnose root causes (estimation, scope, capacity, ownership, quality, or dependencies).

  • Challenge weak plans, unrealistic estimates, unclear ownership, and superficial status reporting.

  • Validate that reported progress reflects real engineering output.

  • Improve planning and forecasting discipline, moving teams from optimistic plans to evidence-based delivery.

  • Work with QA and engineering leads to make quality visible as part of delivery — tracking escaped bugs, rework, and release readiness, and supporting consistent Definition of Ready / Definition of Done and quality gates.

  • Track cross-team dependencies, ensure blockers are owned and resolved, and run clear, fact-based escalation paths.

  • Build a clear understanding of each external team’s composition, role coverage, seniority mix, ownership areas, and capability gaps.

  • Identify where delivery or quality issues are caused by team setup, missing ownership, skill gaps, low allocation, weak technical leadership, or unclear requirements.

  • Ensure external teams follow agreed company delivery rules, documentation expectations, engineering standards, quality gates, and reporting practices.

  • Build vendor/team delivery scorecards covering predictability, quality, responsiveness, planning accuracy, delivery reliability, and escalation patterns.

  • Create fact-based escalation paths when external teams repeatedly miss commitments, provide weak delivery evidence, or fall below agreed quality expectations.

  • Communicate delivery status, risks, and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, translating delivery issues into business impact.

What We’re Looking For

  • 7+ years in software delivery, technical/engineering delivery management, technical program management, or engineering leadership.

  • Proven experience managing delivery across multiple external teams, vendors, or distributed partners.

  • Experience overseeing delivery across engineering teams, vendors, or delivery groups of roughly 20–35 people.

  • Exposure to a few different business models or product environments (rather than narrow specialization) is a strong plus.

  • Strong grasp of software development lifecycles, agile delivery, estimation, release planning, QA workflows, and engineering team dynamics.

  • Ability to build delivery reporting and analysis, and to read teams accurately — including spotting gaps hidden behind tidy reporting.

  • Strong delivery metrics fluency: planned vs. actual, cycle time, throughput, escaped bugs, rework, blocked work, and predictability.

  • Risk and dependency management.

  • Excellent communication with both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Hands-on with delivery and engineering tools such as Jira, GitHub, Confluence, Linear, or Azure DevOps.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in multi-product SaaS environments and companies dependent on external engineering partners.

  • Experience building vendor scorecards or delivery performance frameworks.

  • Experience introducing the Definition of Ready/Done, release checklists, or quality gates.

How We Work

We’re fully remote and distributed across time zones. We default to async, communicate in writing, and trust people to deliver outcomes, not log hours. Decisions are transparent, ownership is clear, and your work is visible from day one.

Interview Process

We've designed our interview process to be transparent, respectful of your time, and a genuine two-way conversation, we want to get to know you, and we want you to get to know us. You'll always know what stage you're at, what to expect next, and roughly how long things will take.

  • Initial screen with our Talent Acquisition Team - 30 min

  • Technical interview with our Hiring Manager - 60 min

  • Take-home assessment - Estimated effort: 2–4 hours

  • Final Interview with the CTO - 60 min

What We Offer

  • Remote-first: work from anywhere in the world, no relocation required.

  • Flexible hours: we measure outcomes, not time at a desk.

  • Unlimited PTO: take the time you need to rest, recharge, and do your best work.

  • Learning & development budget: courses, books, conferences, certifications, whatever helps you grow.

  • Home office & wellness allowance: a dedicated budget to set up your workspace and support your health.

  • A small, senior, collaborative team where your work is visible and your decisions matter.

  • The chance to build products used by millions of people across 160+ countries.

Equal Opportunity

Progress Partners is an equal opportunity employer, and we’re serious about building a diverse, inclusive team. We welcome applications from people of all genders, gender identities and expressions, sexual orientations, ages, ethnicities, nationalities, religions, disabilities, neurotypes, family situations, socioeconomic backgrounds, and life experiences.

We hire on skills, experience, potential, and values fit. never on protected characteristics. If you need accommodations during the application or interview process, just let us know.

title: Sociaal Psychiatrisch Verpleegkundige (SPV) Vluchtelingenprogramma Zuid
description:
Zo werk jij

Voor wie jij er als sociaal psychiatrisch verpleegkundige bent? Vluchtelingen met psychische en psychiatrische klachten, waarbij vaak meerdere factoren tegelijk een rol spelen. Denk aan traumatische ervaringen, verlies, onzekerheid over de toekomst en de impact van migratie en verblijf in een nieuw land. Binnen het Vluchtelingenprogramma Zuid kijk je daarom verder dan alleen de psychiatrische klachten. Je hebt oog voor de culturele, sociale en maatschappelijke context waarin iemand leeft en wat die betekent voor herstel en behandeling.

Als SPV verbind je behandeling en begeleiding met de leefwereld van de patiënt. Je bouwt aan vertrouwen, brengt de situatie zorgvuldig in kaart en zoekt samen met de patiënt en het multidisciplinaire team naar wat nodig en haalbaar is. Daarbij krijg je te maken met uiteenlopende achtergronden en hulpvragen. Dat vraagt om nieuwsgierigheid, flexibiliteit en het vermogen om aan te sluiten zonder aannames te doen.

Vanuit jouw expertise en persoonlijke talenten geef jij vorm aan de functie van SPV. De belangrijkste taken en verantwoordelijkheden zijn voor jou bekend terrein. Wat de functie binnen het Vluchtelingenprogramma Zuid bijzonder maakt is:

  • uitvoeren van intakes, psychiatrisch verpleegkundige diagnostiek en behandelingen en bijdragen aan het behandelplan.

  • begeleiden en behandelen van patiënten, waarbij je aandacht hebt voor zowel psychiatrische problematiek als de sociale en maatschappelijke omstandigheden.

  • signaleren van veranderingen in het psychiatrisch toestandsbeeld en waar nodig interveniëren.

  • samenwerken met naasten, ketenpartners en andere betrokken organisaties rondom de patiënt.

  • bijdragen aan cultuursensitieve zorg en samen met collega's zoeken naar een aanpak die aansluit bij de achtergrond en situatie van de patiënt.

Je werkt zelfstandig vanuit je eigen vakgebied, maar staat er niet alleen voor. Juist bij complexe problematiek is de samenwerking binnen het multidisciplinaire team belangrijk. Je brengt jouw sociaalpsychiatrische blik in en draagt bij aan zorg waarin de patiënt als mens en zijn of haar volledige context centraal staan.

Jouw team

Jouw nieuwe collega's van het Vluchtelingenprogramma Zuid werken vanuit Amersfoort. Het programma is onderdeel van GGz Centraal in de regio Eemland en biedt specialistische geestelijke gezondheidszorg aan vluchtelingen met psychische en psychiatrische problematiek.

Binnen het team komen psychiatrie, trauma, cultuur en maatschappelijke omstandigheden samen. Dat maakt het werk inhoudelijk breed en vraagt om verschillende professionele perspectieven. Je werkt multidisciplinair en stemt waar nodig af met andere zorgverleners en organisaties die rondom de patiënt betrokken zijn.

Samen werken jullie aan zorg die niet alleen deskundig is, maar ook aansluit bij de achtergrond, ervaringen en actuele leefomstandigheden van iedere patiënt.

Wij zorgen voor jou

Werk dat ertoe doet en waarin je jouw expertise als SPV kunt inzetten voor een bijzondere en diverse doelgroep. We zorgen ook goed voor jou. Je krijgt bij GGz Centraal:

  • een bruto maandsalaris tussen € 4.000,- en € 5.294,- (CAO GGZ, functiegroep 55) o.b.v. 36 uur;

  • een contract voor 28-36 uur per week voor onbepaalde tijd. We werken vanuit vertrouwen, dus je krijgt bij ons meteen een vast contract;

  • een eindejaarsuitkering en een vakantietoeslag van 8,33%.

  • 166 verlofuren en 35 levensfase-uren o.b.v. 36 uur. Zo willen we bijdragen aan een goede werk-privébalans.

  • de mogelijkheid om via de WKR fiscaalvriendelijk een (elektrische) fiets of extra vakantiedagen te kopen.

  • een jaarlijks balansbudget van €1.000,- naar rato. Dit budget kun je besteden aan iets waar jij blij van wordt. Denk aan een cursus, extra salaris of verlofuren, aan jou de keuze

  • een lease fiets via Lease a Bike. Hiermee stimuleren we duurzaam en gezond woon-werkverkeer;

  • de ruimte om jezelf professioneel en persoonlijk te ontwikkelen via opleidingen en trainingen.

Onze arbeidsvoorwaarden zijn conform de CAO GGZ. Heb je vragen? Laat het ons weten.

Dit breng je mee

Je bent een SPV die gemakkelijk verbinding maakt met mensen met verschillende achtergronden en levensverhalen. Je kunt omgaan met complexe situaties en blijft daarbij kijken naar wat iemand nodig heeft. Verschillen in taal, cultuur of referentiekader maken je nieuwsgierig en je bent bereid je eigen perspectief kritisch te blijven bekijken.

Daarnaast heb je:

  • een afgeronde opleiding tot sociaal psychiatrisch verpleegkundige en een geldige BIG-registratie.

  • kennis van psychiatrische ziektebeelden en ervaring met complexe psychiatrische problematiek.

  • affiniteit met vluchtelingenzorg, transculturele psychiatrie en/of traumagerelateerde problematiek.

  • het vermogen om zelfstandig te werken én actief de samenwerking binnen en buiten het behandelteam op te zoeken.

Wie zijn wij?

Elk jaar rekenen zo’n 25.000 patiënten op ons als de specialist in geestelijke gezondheidszorg in midden Nederland. Vanuit verschillende locaties, binnen de thuissetting én online, bieden we specialistische hulp aan mensen met psychische problemen, in alle fasen van hun leven.

Ontdek meer over GGz Centraal als werkgever en over onze visie en missie.

In regio Eemland bieden we vanuit onder andere Amersfoort een breed aanbod aan specialistische ggz. Binnen deze regio werken verschillende teams en expertises samen om patiënten zo passend mogelijk te behandelen. Het Vluchtelingenprogramma Zuid is daar onderdeel van en richt zich specifiek op psychiatrische zorg voor vluchtelingen.

Solliciteren

Wil je meer weten over deze functie of het Vluchtelingenprogramma Zuid? Neem dan contact op met Ermie van Bekkum, teammanager, via 06 3061 2757. Voor overige vragen helpt de recruiter je graag verder op weg.

Kom je graag eerst sfeer proeven? Een dagdeel meelopen is mogelijk als onderdeel van de sollicitatieprocedure.

Kom je bij ons werken, dan checken we standaard referenties en vragen we je om een actuele Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag (VOG). Natuurlijk vergoeden wij deze kosten.

title: Product Specialist
description:
PRODUCT SPECIALIST

Agent-ready specifications and end-to-end quality ownership in a three-person AI-native delivery squad

Role

Product Specialist

Function

AI-Native Delivery Squad — Product & Quality

Experience

8–12 years, including 3+ years in a combined specification and quality-ownership role

Location

[Location] — hybrid, with overlap into client business hours

Engagement

Full-time · small-squad delivery on a fixed-timeline platform build

Reports to

Delivery Lead / Architect-Orchestrator

About the role

We deliver platform builds with small AI-native squads. Instead of a large team writing production code by hand, a three-person squad specifies the work, programs and supervises AI coding agents, and verifies everything those agents produce. The agents are the workforce; the squad orchestrates and assures.

The Product Specialist owns what gets built and whether it is right. You turn business and partner requirements into specifications precise enough for an agent to implement without ambiguity, then accept the resulting output against intent before the squad ships it. You also own functional, integration and end-to-end quality for the platform.

There is no junior tier and no layer of people writing tickets beneath you. Every specification you write is executed at speed, and every gap in it surfaces within hours. This role suits someone who writes with precision, is comfortable saying an increment is not acceptable, and wants to work at the front of AI-assisted delivery rather than read about it.

Key responsibilities

Specification ownership

  • Convert business, partner and regulatory requirements into agent-ready specifications — user need, acceptance criteria, API contracts, state transitions, data models, edge cases and negative paths — with no ambiguity left for an agent to resolve on its own.

  • Own the baseline product specification, the journey and state-machine models, and the acceptance-criteria specification set that serve as executable input to AI coding assistants.

  • Build and maintain a spec-driven backlog, groomed continuously to stay ahead of agent throughput on a compressed delivery timeline (single-week discovery, multi-week AI-assisted build).

  • Own requirement traceability end to end — requirement to specification to build to test to sign-off — and produce the traceability evidence pack used at each quality gate.

  • Specify partner integration contracts alongside the architect: request and response schemas, webhook payloads, callback semantics, error and retry behavior, idempotency rules and correlation identifiers.

Accepting and governing agent output

  • Accept AI-generated output against intent before the squad ships. Decide per increment whether output is fit to ship, needs rework, or must be rejected.

  • Diagnose specification weakness when agents drift — tighten the specification rather than patch the output.

  • Work inside defined agent autonomy boundaries, escalating anything that touches personal or sensitive data, consent wording, authentication and session handling, or third-party partner integrations to human decision.

  • Contribute to the reusable specification, prompt and playbook library so that patterns proven on one journey are reused across the next.

Functional, integration and end-to-end quality

  • Own functional, integration and end-to-end test coverage for the platform — this is a specification-and-quality role, not a pure product role.

  • Design and execute business-rules validation, partner contract and integration testing (schema validation, webhook signature handling, retries, idempotency, correlation IDs), end-to-end journey testing and negative-path coverage.

  • Apply AI-enabled test tooling across the lifecycle: requirement intelligence and gap detection, AI test-case generation, AI-powered API automation, and browser automation via Playwright or an equivalent MCP-driven tool.

  • Coordinate non-functional test coverage — resilience, disaster recovery, accessibility and observability — and manage handover of load and security testing where the client owns those activities.

  • Drive the quality gates: build-ready, integration-ready, UAT-ready and go-live-ready. Own the evidence that each gate has been met.

  • Produce quality reporting the squad and client act on — defect clustering, coverage against traced requirements, and release-confidence and stability summaries.

Client and partner engagement

  • Run demos, backlog re-prioritisation and specification traceability reviews with client and partner leads on a fixed cadence.

  • Join weekly architecture and integration checkpoints with third-party partner engineering teams; drive resolution of contract and schema issues to a decision.

  • Own client validation of acceptance criteria and secure formal UAT sign-off.

  • Support go-live readiness, handover documentation and warranty-period defect triage.

Must-have skills and experience

  • 8–12 years across product ownership, business analysis or QA leadership, with at least 3 years in a role combining specification ownership with hands-on quality ownership.

  • Demonstrable ability to write specifications precise enough to drive automated implementation: acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then form, state machines, data models and API contracts.

  • Hands-on with OpenAPI/Swagger — able to read, review and specify REST contracts, webhook payloads and error contracts without needing an engineer to interpret them.

  • Strong integration testing background against third-party APIs: schema validation, webhook verification, retry and idempotency behaviour, correlation and reconciliation of asynchronous events.

  • End-to-end test design and hands-on automation exposure with Playwright, Cypress or an equivalent framework.

  • Working fluency with AI coding and testing assistants (for example Claude or GitHub Copilot) as everyday delivery tools — including prompt discipline, context management and disciplined verification of generated output.

  • Experience delivering in regulated, privacy-sensitive environments with explicit consent capture, data minimisation, masking, role-based access control and audit-trail obligations.

  • Experience with conversational or messaging-channel products — WhatsApp Business Platform or an equivalent channel via providers such as Infobip or Twilio.

  • Comfortable operating in a small squad with no junior tier, taking direct accountability for scope, quality and sign-off.

  • Excellent written English. Much of the deliverable in this role is precise prose.

Good to have

  • Azure exposure — Azure SQL Database, Blob Storage, Key Vault, Azure Monitor and Application Insights, OpenTelemetry-based tracing.

  • Enough familiarity with Node.js, NestJS and TypeScript to review generated code and reason about workflow and state orchestration — you are not expected to build it.

  • OCR and document-extraction workflows, including user correction flows for low-confidence extractions.

  • Experience with spec-driven or agent-based delivery practices — engineering guardrail files, MCP context servers, prompt and skill libraries, human review gates.

  • Domain background in regulated consumer services — healthcare services, insurance, financial services or similar.

  • Certification such as CSPO, CSM, or ISTQB Advanced.

What success looks like

  • Discovery week: baseline product and technical specifications, state and data models, acceptance-criteria specifications and the spec-driven backlog are signed off, and agent guardrail guidance is agreed.

  • Build phase: specifications stay ahead of agent throughput; integration and end-to-end coverage tracks each increment as it lands; build-ready, integration-ready and UAT-ready gates pass on schedule with traceable evidence.

  • Release: UAT sign-off secured, traceability and hardening evidence pack complete, handover and knowledge-transfer documentation accepted by the client.

How we work

  • Throughput is measured in increments shipped and verified, not story points estimated.

  • Status, velocity and progress reporting are largely generated — you spend your time on specification and verification, not on administration.

  • Verification is the core skill. The squad ships only what it can verify, and every merge and release is a human decision.

  • Design system, platform engineering and engineering management are shared functions across squads rather than embedded in the squad.

description:

EMPACT- Suicide Prevention Center, part of the La Frontera Arizona family, is an industry-leading non-profit organization dedicated to providing valued community services and resources for behavioral health counseling, crisis intervention, and suicide prevention since 1987. We are an EEO/AA Employer.

What you’ll do:

The Trauma Healing Therapist provides direct psychotherapy, individually and in group settings, as well as, crisis stabilization, and other services to individuals and families whose lives have been impacted by crimes, including, but not limited to, sexual assault, domestic violence, human trafficking, attempted homicide, stalking, etc. using a Systems based approach to interventions.

This position will be Monday - Friday based at Glendale Family Advocacy Center two days per week and at EMPACT Tempe Children's Center the rest of the week.

*On Call component required. *Crisis Differential provided.

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Provides direct community based psychotherapy for the purpose of assessment, diagnosis and treatment with follow-up contact for victims of crime in both individual and group settings. Clientele includes youth, adults and families. Identifies victims’ personal advocacy, provisions & assistance needs including appropriate in-house & community referrals. Makes mandatory reports to appropriate authorities regarding child or vulnerable adult abuse or neglect.
  • Coordinates communication with other departments in the agency for continuity of care. Collaborates with hotline staff, trauma advocates and therapists, plus community agencies to provide crisis intervention and de-escalation/stabilization of high intensity trauma symptoms on scene, risk assessment for danger to self or others, transportation, victim support and/or supervision, psycho-education about trauma symptomology, parenting training, behavior management training and assistance.
  • Ensures quality service delivery including clinical care and all associated documentation and complies with the agency’s standard of care for service delivery. Includes providing mobile crisis assessment, intervention services, and in home support services to clients throughout Maricopa and surrounding counties.

At time of hire, a 3-year state driving record with no major infractions or excessive driving violations/tickets is required.

title: Entry Level- DSP Engineer (Onsite- Aberdeen, Maryland)
description:
ENTRY-LEVEL DIGITAL SIGNAL PROCESSING ENGINEER

xG and Mixed Signal Product Development | Technical Services

About the opportunity

Fairwinds Technologies is continuously looking for curious, hands-on early-career engineers who want to apply digital signal processing theory to real radios, RF systems, embedded platforms, and operationally relevant test environments. In this role, you may support either our xG or Mixed Signal product development team, or technical-services contracts aligned with those product areas.

You will work alongside experienced DSP, FPGA, RF, software, systems, and test engineers to model, implement, integrate, measure, and improve signal-processing capabilities. Assignments may span internal product development and customer-funded research, integration, test, demonstration, and field-support activities. The position is designed to build practical engineering depth while giving an early-career engineer exposure to the full lifecycle from algorithm concept through measured performance.

What you will do

  • Develop, simulate, analyze, and test digital signal processing algorithms for communications, sensing, RF test, and signal-conditioning applications.
  • Use MATLAB, Simulink, Python, or comparable engineering tools to model signals, evaluate algorithm performance, visualize results, and automate analysis.
  • Implement and validate filtering, modulation and demodulation, synchronization, channelization, resampling, spectral analysis, detection, estimation, and related DSP functions as assigned.
  • Analyze time-domain and frequency-domain data from simulations, laboratory instruments, radios, channel emulators, and prototype hardware.
  • Support translation of algorithms into embedded software or FPGA-oriented implementations in collaboration with software and FPGA engineers.
  • Develop repeatable test methods, reference models, test vectors, acceptance criteria, and automated data-processing workflows.
  • Assist with system integration involving radios, modems, data converters, RF front ends, coherent signal paths, networked test equipment, and embedded Linux platforms.
  • Compare predicted and measured performance, investigate discrepancies, document root causes, and recommend corrective actions.
  • Prepare clear technical documentation, test reports, plots, briefings, and configuration records for product and customer-funded activities.
  • Participate in laboratory and field testing, demonstrations, design reviews, and multidisciplinary troubleshooting.

Technology and mission areas

Depending on assignment, you may contribute in one or more of the following areas:

  • xG wireless systems, including 5G, non-terrestrial networking, software-defined radio, tactical communications, radio integration, and performance characterization.
  • Mixed Signal products, including Global Link and EchoPhase-related capabilities, channel emulation, coherent combining, wideband signal processing, and FPGA/DSP hardware interfaces.
  • Waveform analysis, RF frequency translation, channel effects, synchronization, calibration, signal quality, interference, and link-performance assessment.
  • Ruggedized mission modules and edge systems that combine compute, networking, radio, RF, and signal-processing functions.
  • Government-funded R&D and technical-services contracts involving algorithm development, integration, test, documentation, demonstrations, and field support.

Minimum qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Applied Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a closely related technical field, completed or expected before start date.
  • Coursework, laboratory, internship, capstone, research, or personal-project experience in digital signal processing, communications, controls, image processing, acoustics, radar, or a related analytical discipline.
  • Working knowledge of core DSP concepts such as sampling, aliasing, discrete-time systems, convolution, digital filtering, Fourier transforms, spectra, noise, and signal-to-noise ratio.
  • Experience using MATLAB, Python, Simulink, GNU Radio, or another numerical modeling and analysis environment.
  • Basic programming ability and willingness to learn the software and hardware interfaces needed to move algorithms into practical systems.
  • Ability to apply structured problem solving, interpret measured data, communicate assumptions, and document results clearly.
  • Ability to collaborate in a multidisciplinary engineering environment and satisfy customer, site-access, export-control, and security requirements associated with assigned work.

Preferred, not required

  • Exposure to digital communications topics such as modulation, coding, synchronization, equalization, channel estimation, link budgets, or error-rate analysis.
  • Experience with software-defined radio platforms, GNU Radio, RF laboratory equipment, data-acquisition systems, or recorded in-phase and quadrature data.
  • Familiarity with fixed-point arithmetic, real-time processing, FPGA development concepts, HDL, embedded C or C++, or hardware-in-the-loop testing.
  • Coursework or project experience in wireless communications, 5G/LTE, non-terrestrial networks, radar, electronic warfare, satellite communications, coherent systems, or RF test and measurement.
  • Exposure to Git, Linux, automated testing, CI/CD, technical plotting, report generation, or reproducible analysis workflows.

What success looks like

  • First 90 days: learn the assigned product or program, modeling environment, laboratory workflow, signal chain, and performance objectives; complete scoped analysis and test tasks with mentoring.
  • First 6 months: independently build or modify a reference model, analyze measured data, automate a repeatable workflow, and communicate conclusions through clear plots and documentation.
  • First year: own a defined DSP algorithm, analysis capability, performance model, or verification activity and become a dependable contributor across algorithm, software, FPGA, RF, and test boundaries.

Why join Fairwinds Technologies

  • Work on products and customer-funded R&D activities within the same technical domain, connecting analytical concepts with hardware, measured data, and operational use cases.
  • Gain broad exposure to wireless systems, RF hardware, software-defined radios, channel emulation, coherent systems, FPGA interfaces, embedded computing, laboratory integration, and field testing.
  • Learn from experienced multidisciplinary engineers while receiving meaningful modeling, implementation, and test responsibilities early in your career.
  • Join a growing technology organization expanding its xG and Mixed Signal portfolios and strengthening repeatable product-development practices.

How to apply

Submit your resume and, if available, links or short descriptions for relevant code, MATLAB or Python analyses, laboratory work, capstone projects, research, internships, technical papers, or portfolios. Tell us what problem you addressed, what you personally developed or analyzed, how you validated the result, and what you learned.


Compensation- Salary

At Fairwinds, we consider many factors when it comes to compensation, including the scope of the position as well as your background and experience. Base pay may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, location and experience. Additional incentives may be provided as part of the compensation package, in addition to a range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits.

Position Type/Expected Hours of Work

This is a full time, exempt position.

Must be eligible to work in the US.

  • Monitor/test wash water, sanitizer concentration, pH levels, cooler temperatures, and other processing control points.

  • Oversee product traceability within hold and rework programs.
  • Candle shell egg samples for quality.

  • Experience managing domestic and international freight movements in a complex, high-volume environment.

title: CDL-A Rerail Operator
description:
CDL-A Rerail Operator

Location: Minneapolis, MN
Job Type: Full-Time | Direct Hire
Starting Pay: $26.00/hour — higher pay available depending on experience
Benefits: Full-time benefits
Schedule: 40 hours guaranteed weekly + significant overtime
Availability: 24/7 emergency on-call

Position Overview

We are hiring a Class A CDL Rerail Operator to assist with railroad emergency response and recovery operations. This position combines equipment operation, transportation, material handling, and hands-on field work.

Driving is only a small part of the position. When not responding to emergencies, employees may assist with equipment maintenance, preventive maintenance, and safety training.

Responsibilities

  • Complete pre- and post-trip inspections of trucks, trailers, and equipment in accordance with DOT requirements.
  • Transport equipment, machinery, and materials safely to and from work locations.
  • Inspect loads and confirm permits for oversized or overweight equipment.
  • Participate in daily work planning and safety briefings.
  • Load, unload, move, and stage equipment and materials for rerailing and railroad operations.
  • Assist with train rerailing, load adjustment and transfer, railroad car maintenance/repair, track maintenance, repair, and new construction.
  • Help assemble, inspect, and operate cranes and other equipment.
  • Assist with rigging and connecting chains, cables, and winches.
  • Operate equipment such as:
    • Cranes
    • Backhoes
    • Bulldozers
    • Excavators
    • Front-end loaders
    • Grapple trucks
    • Dump trucks
    • Rail-bound equipment
    • Tractors
    • Skid-steer loaders
    • Use hydraulic tools, welding equipment, cutting torches, electrical tools, and common hand tools.
    • Monitor vehicles and equipment to help maintain safe and reliable operation.
    • Perform and document minor equipment and vehicle servicing.
    • Assist with equipment disassembly, loading, and cleanup after assignments.
    • Restock vehicles and equipment with parts, components, and supplies.
    • Maintain organized work areas, vehicles, tools, and equipment.
    • Follow all safety policies and procedures.
    • Assist other departments or crews as needed.

Requirements

  • Valid Class A Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) with a good driving record.
  • Construction, equipment operation, or other physically demanding labor experience.
  • Ability to safely operate heavy equipment.
  • Ability to complete required qualification, training, and safety programs.
  • Must be available 24/7 for emergency response, including weekends and holidays.
  • Comfortable performing physical field work and working extended hours when required.

Preferred Experience

  • 3+ years of heavy equipment operating experience, including:
    • Backhoe
    • Bulldozer
    • Excavator
    • Front-end loader
    • Grapple truck
    • Rail-bound equipment
    • Tractor
    • Skid-steer loader
    • Equivalent combination of training and experience may be considered.

Schedule & Compensation

  • 40 hours guaranteed per week.
  • Typical workweeks average 60+ hours, with some weeks reaching approximately 70 hours.
  • Hours outside Monday–Friday, 7:00 AM–4:00 PM are paid at time-and-a-half overtime rates.
  • Additional compensation may include per diem, hotel expenses for travel, and layover pay, when applicable.
  • 24/7 on-call availability is required for emergency response.

Pre-Employment Requirements

  • Drug screening

title: Sociaal Psychiatrisch Verpleegkundige (SPV) Poli Stemming & Angst
description:
Zo werk jij

Voor wie jij er als sociaal psychiatrisch verpleegkundige bent? Volwassenen met stemmings- en angststoornissen die specialistische behandeling nodig hebben. Je combineert verpleegkundige en psychiatrische expertise en kijkt daarbij verder dan alleen de klachten. Ook het dagelijks functioneren, de sociale omgeving en wat iemand nodig heeft om duurzaam verder te komen, krijgen een belangrijke plek in de behandeling.

Binnen de polikliniek bieden we zowel poliklinische als deeltijdbehandeling. Behandelingen vinden individueel en in groepsverband plaats en bestaan onder andere uit cognitieve gedragstherapie, schematherapie, zelfbeeldtraining, activeringsgroepen en medicamenteuze behandeling.

Vanuit jouw expertise en persoonlijke talenten geef jij vorm aan de functie van sociaal psychiatrisch verpleegkundige. De belangrijkste taken en verantwoordelijkheden zijn voor jou bekend terrein. Wat de functie bij GGz Centraal bijzonder maakt is:

  • het begeleiden en behandelen van patiënten met uiteenlopende stemmings- en angststoornissen;

  • het in kaart brengen van psychiatrische, verpleegkundige en sociaal-maatschappelijke factoren en deze vertalen naar passende behandelinterventies;

  • het bewaken van de voortgang van de behandeling en signaleren van veranderingen in het psychiatrisch toestandsbeeld;

  • het betrekken van naasten en het sociale netwerk wanneer dit bijdraagt aan het herstel;

  • het intensief samenwerken met verschillende disciplines binnen de poliklinische en deeltijdbehandeling.

Jouw team

Jouw nieuwe collega’s van de polikliniek Stemmings- en Angststoornissen kijken ernaar uit om je te ontmoeten. Samen met jou als sociaal psychiatrisch verpleegkundige bieden we specialistische behandeling aan volwassenen met stemmings- en angststoornissen. De polikliniek maakt deel uit van GGz Centraal in regio Eemland. Een brede regio waarin veel verschillende vormen van specialistische ggz samenkomen. Herstelgerichte zorg en goede samenwerking binnen én buiten GGz Centraal staan daarbij centraal. We blijven onze zorg ontwikkelen en zoeken naar mogelijkheden om deze verder te verbeteren. Als professional krijg je ruimte om vanuit jouw expertise bij te dragen aan de behandeling én aan de ontwikkeling van de zorg.

We bieden zowel poliklinische behandeling als intensievere deeltijdbehandeling, individueel en in groepsverband. Wat ons team kenmerkt? De multidisciplinaire samenwerking en de combinatie van verschillende behandelvormen waarmee we aansluiten bij wat een patiënt nodig heeft. Jouw nieuwe werkplek? De polikliniek is gevestigd aan het Smallepad 30B in Amersfoort.

Wij zorgen voor jou

Werk dat er toe doet en waar je van betekenis bent, dat is alvast onze eerste belofte. Omdat we een grote organisatie zijn met verschillende werklocaties kunnen we inspelen op ontwikkelwensen en voorkeuren qua functie-inhoud, type behandelprogramma en woon-werkafstand. We zien wie je bent en wat je kan. Als [functienaam] bij GGz Centraal kun je in ieder geval rekenen op:

  • een bruto maandsalaris tussen € 4.000,- en € 5.294,- op basis van 36 uur, volgens de CAO GGZ (FWG 55). Bereken hier jouw netto salaris;

  • een contract voor 28 tot 36 uur per week voor onbepaalde tijd. We werken vanuit vertrouwen, dus je krijgt bij ons meteen een vast contract;

  • een eindejaarsuitkering en een vakantietoeslag van 8,33%.

  • 166 verlofuren en 35 levensfase-uren o.b.v. 36 uur. Zo willen we bijdragen aan een goede werk-privébalans.

  • de mogelijkheid om via de WKR fiscaalvriendelijk een (elektrische) fiets of extra vakantiedagen te kopen.

  • een jaarlijks balansbudget van €1.000,- naar rato. Dit budget kun je besteden aan iets waar jij blij van wordt. Denk aan een cursus, extra
    salaris of verlofuren, aan jou de keuze.

  • een lease fiets via Lease a Bike. Hiermee stimuleren we duurzaam en gezond woon-werkverkeer.

  • de ruimte om jezelf professioneel en persoonlijk te ontwikkelen via opleidingen en trainingen.

Onze arbeidsvoorwaarden zijn conform de CAO GGZ. Heb je vragen? Laat het ons weten.

Dit breng je mee

Je brengt verpleegkundige expertise samen met kennis van psychiatrische problematiek en hebt oog voor de invloed van iemands sociale omgeving. Daarnaast beschik je over:

  • een afgeronde opleiding tot sociaal psychiatrisch verpleegkundige;

  • een geldige BIG-registratie als verpleegkundige;

  • kennis van en affiniteit met de behandeling van volwassenen met psychiatrische problematiek;

  • het vermogen om zelfstandig te werken én actief samen te werken binnen een multidisciplinair team.

Wie zijn wij?

Elk jaar rekenen zo’n 25.000 patiënten op ons als de specialist in geestelijke gezondheidszorg in midden Nederland. Vanuit verschillende locaties, binnen de thuissetting én online, bieden we specialistische hulp aan mensen met psychische problemen, in alle fasen van hun leven.

Ontdek meer over GGz Centraal als werkgever en over onze visie en missie.

In regio Eemland bieden we specialistische geestelijke gezondheidszorg aan kinderen, jongeren, volwassenen en ouderen. We werken herstelgericht en organiseren de zorg zoveel mogelijk rondom de patiënt. Daarbij werken we nauw samen tussen onze verschillende behandelteams en met partners in de regio. We blijven onze zorg ontwikkelen en verbeteren, waarbij professionals ruimte krijgen om vanuit hun expertise bij te dragen aan goede en passende zorg.

Solliciteren

Wil je meer informatie over de vacature? Neem contact op met Annelies Rooiman, teammanager via 06 1285 3052. Voor overige vragen helpt de recruiter je graag verder op weg. Kom je graag eerst sfeer proeven? Een dagdeel is mogelijk als onderdeel van de sollicitatieprocedure. Als we dé geschikte kandidaat hebben gevonden, sluiten we de vacature eerder. Hebben we onze match nog niet gevonden? Dan zoeken we nog wat langer door.

Kom je bij ons werken, dan checken we standaard referenties en vragen we je om een actuele Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag (VOG). Natuurlijk vergoeden wij deze kosten.

title: Advisor, Supporter Engagement & Fundraising (P3)
location: Fairfield, Town of, Connecticut, United States
description:
Save the Children

For over 100 years, Save the Children has been fighting for the rights of children. The right to a healthy start in life. To have access to education. To be in a safe environment, protected from harm. We work in some of the world’s hardest-to-reach places – over 100 countries, including the U.S. No matter what your role is, when you join Save the Children, you’re creating positive, irreversible change for children, and the future we all share.

The Role

As the Advisor, Supporter Engagement and Fundraising, you’ll be integral to our work in helping vulnerable children achieve a brighter future. You will be responsible for developing strategies to engage and retain supporters and manage all aspects of the direct response marketing retention & fundraising program; mainly focused on direct mail.

You will collaborate with key stakeholders to ensure a cohesive supporter experience across all channels and will be accountable for maximizing our mission support revenue and delivering on both short-term key performance indicators and long-term metrics such as lifetime value and retention. You will collaborate with key stakeholders to identify and implement ambitious, innovative, and effective marketing strategies and engagement opportunities that will enable us to build a highly engaged audience that will drive impact for children.

Location

Hybrid – Washington DC, Fairfield, CT or Lexington, KY office locations

What You’ll Be Doing (Essential Duties)
*not inclusive of all role responsibilities. May be subject to change

Strategy & Campaign Management (30%):

  • Collaborate with partners to develop and oversee strategies to grow and optimize the mass market supporter retention and fundraising direct marketing program (primarily through direct mail) with collaboration from internal stakeholders.
  • Develop and implement strategies that increase donor retention, lifetime value, mid-level and legacy progression, and long-term supporter engagement.
  • Manage relationships and performance of creative agency, production, and data-processing partners to ensure high-quality execution and continuous optimization.
  • Manage implementation of annual and campaign-level plans, including house-file mailings, welcome journeys, sustainer conversion, reactivation, cultivation, emergency response fundraising, and donor development programs for priority audiences and segments including planned giving. Develop and manage schedules with printers, creative agencies, data processors, and internal teams, ensuring campaigns are executed successfully and timely.
  • Create and implement segmentation and testing strategies on all campaigns.
  • Represent direct mail fundraising during integrated campaign planning and cross-functional initiatives.
  • Advise and inform team of industry best practices and stay abreast of trends.

Campaign Execution (35%):

  • Lead the day-to-day execution of direct response marketing campaigns; mostly as it relates to direct mail.
  • Streamline processes and maximize operational effectiveness to increase fundraising, retention, and reactivation metrics.
  • Track all creative updates and changes, facilitating the flow between Save the Children and external vendors.
  • Obtain project/campaign/material legal approvals by acting as lead contact and knowledge base for legal approval process.
  • Manage setup of campaign matrix, appeals, and data requests for our IT department.
  • Manage lettershop instructions and ensure all data processing and scheduling of campaigns are executed accurately with high operational performance and efficient interdepartmental collaboration.

Performance Analysis and Support (25%):

  • Responsible for budget creation and monitoring spend, including determining appropriate level of investments to deliver on fundraising goals.
  • Maintain regular deliverables (reports, dashboards, benchmark reports, etc.) on key metrics to continually improve program and measure strategy effectiveness.
  • Author monthly direct mail channel report for department – inclusive of acquisition and retention campaign performance
  • Provide recommendations to senior leadership and extended team on direct mail campaign strategy and other supporter cultivation and integrative efforts based on short term key performance indicators and long-term metrics such as lifetime value and retention.
  • Complete ad-hoc assignments as assigned.

Staff Management (10%)

  • Supervise the Lead Associate, Sustainer Experience & Retention, who supports journey and campaign efforts for our recurring donor program
  • Train, develop, coach, lead, and supervise staff, clearly communicating organization, division, and department priorities, and how their work contributes to our mission, ensuring that the working environment continually fosters diversity, inclusion, and belonging – supporting Save the Children values.

Required qualifications for the role

  • Minimum of a bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, plus at least 5 years of relevant experience
  • Demonstrated direct mail experience
  • Demonstrated fundraising experience
  • Proven leadership, interpersonal and motivation skills. Able to provide advice, guidance and management of several campaigns and programs
  • Demonstrated ability to successfully deliver work under deadlines and competing priorities, with proven organizational and time management skills
  • Advanced Microsoft Office (Outlook, Work, Excel), and Adobe skills.
  • Ability to work in a cross-cultural environment
  • Professional proficiency in MS Office suite
  • Professional proficiency in spoken and written English
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with individuals and teams at all levels, both internally and externally

Preferred qualifications for the role

  • Previous non-profit experience.
  • Experience with omni-channel campaign planning
  • Experience with Salesforce CRM and Salesforce Marketing Cloud

Compensation

Save the Children is offering the following salary ranges for this position, dependent on candidate location:

  • Geo 1 - NY Metro, DC, and other locations with labor costs significantly above national average: Target Salary for this position is $91,800 - $102,600 base salary
  • Geo 2 - Locations around the US National Labor Cost Average: Target Salary for this position is $83,725 - $93,575 base salary
  • Geo 3 - Locations significantly below the US National Labor Cost Average: Target Salary for this position is $74,800 - $83,600 base salary

The salary ranges listed above are for US based candidates. For candidates located outside of the US, salary ranges will be based on the salary scales of the local employer of record. Actual base salary may vary based on, but not limited to, relevant experience, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location (more information on job structure is available here).

About Us

We are looking to build an inclusive team at Save the Children. We offer a range of outstanding benefits to support this goal:

  • Flexible schedules and time off: Flexible schedules, generous PTO, 11 paid holidays plus 2 floating holidays, and hybrid working opportunities
  • Health: Competitive health care, dental and vision coverage for you and your family
  • Family: A variety of paid leaves: caregiver, parental/adoption, critical child illness, and fertility benefits
  • Employee Rewards Program: Annual merit increases and/or additional incentives for eligible employees
  • Retirement: A retirement savings plan with employer contributions (after one year)
  • Wellness: 15 safety and wellness days annually (if hired on or after July 1, safety and wellness days prorated to 8 days), mental health benefits and support through Calm and company-hosted events
  • Employee Assistance Program: free and confidential assessments, short-term counseling, referrals, and follow-up services
  • Learning & Growth: Access to internal and external learning & development opportunities and mentorships

Click here to learn more about how Save the Children US will invest in you.

Save the Children is committed to conducting its programs and operations in a manner that is safe for the children it serves and helping protect the children with whom we are in contact. All Save the Children representatives are explicitly prohibited from engaging in any activity that may result in any kind of child abuse.

Save the Children is committed to minimizing safety and security risks for our valued employees, ensuring all are given training, support, and information to reduce their risk exposure while maximizing the impact of our programs for children and families. Our shared duty, both agency and individual, is to seek and maintain safe working conditions for all.

title: Technician II - Wind
description:
Technician II - Wind

OnSite Partners is seeking a Technician II perform and lead complex troubleshooting, maintenance, component replacement, and commissioning activities on utility-scale wind turbines and associated collection systems. This role serves as the senior technical resource on site and may provide direction to junior technicians during both scheduled preventive maintenance and unscheduled corrective repairs.

This position requires advanced knowledge of mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, and control systems across multiple voltage classes, along with strong diagnostic and leadership capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead scheduled preventive maintenance on wind turbines
  • Lead troubleshooting of complex turbine faults and recurring system failures
  • Diagnose electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, and control system issues
  • Analyze fault codes, SCADA data, and performance trends
  • Perform root cause analysis and recommend corrective actions
  • Support remote operations and engineering teams with technical expertise
  • Perform work across varying AC and DC voltage classes including:
  • Low-voltage control systems
  • 480V–690V turbine systems
  • Medium-voltage collection systems and switchgear (as qualified)
  • Conduct advanced electrical testing including:
  • Insulation resistance (megger) testing
  • Continuity and phase rotation testing
  • Torque verification
  • Transformer and breaker inspections
  • System Operator on-call duties
  • Lead lockout/tagout (LOTO) and arc-flash safety procedures
  • Assist with protection systems and relay interface troubleshooting
  • Lead major corrective repairs and component replacements
  • Ensure proper torquing, alignment, and commissioning procedures
  • Support turbine commissioning and re-commissioning activities
  • Perform performance testing and system validation
  • Assist with software updates and controller adjustments
  • Provide technical guidance to entry-level and intermediate technicians
  • Lead job safety analyses (JSAs) and daily safety briefings
  • Assist site leadership with planning and scheduling complex work scopes
  • Serve as acting lead technician when required
  • Complete detailed service reports and root cause documentation
  • Maintain compliance with OSHA, NFPA 70E, and site-specific safety standards
  • Ensure adherence to manufacturer specifications and quality standards

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of wind turbine maintenance experience
  • Demonstrated advanced troubleshooting ability
  • Experience with medium-voltage systems
  • Ability to climb turbines (300+ feet) and work at heights
  • Valid driver’s license
  • Ability to pass background check and drug screening

Preferred Qualifications

  • Wind turbine manufacturer training certifications
  • OSHA 30 certification
  • MSHA Part 46 certification
  • NFPA 70E training
  • Experience leading major component exchanges
  • SCADA system familiarity
  • Experience with SEL technology
  • First Aid/CPR certification
  • Previous industrial, construction, or mechanical experience
  • Experience in industrial, utility-scale, or renewable energy environments
  • Working knowledge of NEC and NFPA 70E

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to climb ladders vertically for extended distances
  • Ability to lift 30 pounds
  • Work outdoors in extreme weather conditions
  • Ability to stand, kneel, bend, and work in various physical positions for extended periods

title: Supply Chain Management Student Program
description:
STUDENT PROGRAM FORMAT

This student program follows a format in which participants work remotely during the academic year (September through April) and onsite during the summer (May through August). Remote work must be performed from a location within the United States.

During the academic year, students who reside in the Metro Detroit area are highly encouraged to work onsite at the Stellantis Headquarters and Technology Center in Auburn Hills, Michigan, as their schedules permit.

During the academic year, students are expected to work 24 hours per week during normal business hours, Monday through Friday. Students selected for the program will work with their manager to establish a consistent weekly schedule that fulfills the 24-hour requirement while accommodating their class schedule.

During the summer months (May through August), students are expected to work onsite at the Stellantis Headquarters and Technology Center in Auburn Hills, Michigan. Students may be required to relocate and may work up to 40 hours per week during this period, based on business needs and management discretion. Relocation assistance may be available to students who meet specific eligibility requirements.

Student program cohorts start on a quarterly basis in January, April, June, and September, and students are intended to stay in the program until graduation.

STELLANTIS STUDENT PROGRAM HIGHLIGHTS

The Stellantis Student Program offers a unique alternative to traditional summer internships by providing students with the opportunity to work year-round throughout their academic journey. This continuous engagement allows students to apply their classroom learning in real-world settings on a daily basis, fostering deeper integration within their teams and organizations. As they progress through the program, students are empowered to take on increasing levels of responsibility, gaining valuable experience, and making meaningful contributions along the way.

Students will be assigned to a department based on the candidate's background and skill set. The assignments are project-oriented, meaningful to the department, and allow the student to provide valuable contributions. Students experience a sense of personal accomplishment and learn about the corporate business culture through work assignments, structured activities, and exclusive student networking events.

STUDENT PROGRAM BENEFITS

  • Exposure to cutting-edge projects and technologies
  • Collaborative work environment
  • Mentorship from experienced professionals
  • Networking opportunities with peers and leaders
  • Skill development workshops and training sessions
  • Paid US holidays
  • Stellantis Employee Advantage Vehicle Discount Program
  • Eligible students may be able to participate in the Company Vehicle Employee Lease Program

DEPARTMENT DETAILS

The Supply Chain Management organization manages the flow of parts and materials, works with sales and manufacturing to connect demand to production plans and is responsible for parts and vehicle transportation networks. Supply Chain Management students will experience comprehensive projects while working within one of the following organizations:

  • Demand Planning: This organization is responsible for retail forecasting, vehicle inventory analysis, reporting, validation, and order allocation.
  • Supply: This organization aligns demand plans with production capacities to develop an optimal vehicle production plan. They are responsible for slotting, scheduling and sequencing orders within our manufacturing facilities as well as order execution, releasing, production programming and capacity sizing. In addition, this organization works to resolve production and supplier constraints, material requirement variances, expedite/crisis management and critical part resolution.
  • Transportation: This organization manages parts and vehicle transportation networks and cost management, as well as operating an internal trucking company. This organization also manages inter-regional flow and customs activity by facilitating the inbound and outbound transportation of parts and material between the global regions.
  • Transformation Projects: This organization serves as the single point of contact for coordination and ownership of all supply related activities for new program launches as well as creating main supply chain assumptions and ensuring cross-functional areas are aligned. They also manage vehicle specification, components and options and supplier development and system integrations.
  • Global Supplier Delivery Crisis Management: This organization works to resolve critical part constraints by working with suppliers to develop production and supply plans.
  • Selected candidates will gain industry experience, interface with all levels within our supply chain department and apply their coursework to drive results.

description:

Job Details

Job Title: Art Instructor

Position Summary

The Art Instructor provides support to individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities in a creative, inclusive, and person-centered environment. The Art Instructor also helps promote the studio and creates opportunities for individuals served to engage with the local community. Individual Support and Community Integration

  • Provide individualized support to participants, helping to remove barriers to learning and increase engagement in services.
  • Support individuals in community-based activities in accordance with their service plans and identified goals.
  • Collaborate as a member of a multidisciplinary team to provide holistic, values-based services.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

One of the following is required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Fine Arts, Art Education, Studio Arts, or a related field, plus one (1) year of experience in an art-related discipline; OR
  • High School Diploma or GED equivalent, plus three (3) years of studio practice, including at least one (1) year of experience in an art-related discipline.

Additional Requirements

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications and other relevant technology.
  • Ability to work effectively with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

Working Conditions

  • Work is performed in both office and art studio environments.

The position may involve exposure to:

  • Art materials, dust, fumes, or odors associated with artistic activities.

  • Occasional exposure to cleaning agents and other studio-related materials.

Physical Requirements

  • Occasionally lift and carry supplies and equipment weighing up to 40 pounds.

Medium Work

title: Senior Customer Engineer
description:

The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.

€48,000.00 - €66,000.00

Leixlip,IRL

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits.

As a Field Service Engineer [Customer Engineer] at Applied Materials, you serve as the direct liaison with customers, collaborating closely to install, maintain, and upgrade equipment. You'll use digital analytics for troubleshooting and apply basic diagnostic techniques to assess and address technical issues. Your responsibilities include performing preventative and corrective maintenance on various systems such as electrical, vacuum, mechanical, plasma, hydraulic, and gas systems. Additionally, you'll coordinate and communicate directly with customers to ensure smooth operations and exceptional service.

About the Role

As a Customer Engineer III, you'll play a critical role in supporting some of the world's most advanced semiconductor manufacturing environments. Working directly with customers and cross-functional teams, you'll help maximize equipment performance, uptime, productivity, and operational excellence through the installation, maintenance, and optimization of Applied Materials' leading-edge technologies.

This role offers the opportunity to combine hands-on technical expertise with customer engagement and problem-solving while building a long-term career within a global technology leader. Many of our engineers grow into technical specialist, product support, leadership, installation and ramp, and operational management roles as they develop their careers with Applied Materials.


Key Responsibilities

  • Install, maintain, qualify, and upgrade Applied Materials equipment within customer manufacturing facilities.
  • Diagnose and resolve complex equipment issues through a structured troubleshooting and root-cause approach, escalating when required.
  • Support customers in achieving critical performance objectives related to equipment availability, productivity, and process stability.
  • Collaborate with Senior Customer Engineers and customer stakeholders to understand technology roadmaps, operational priorities, and manufacturing challenges.
  • Perform preventative and corrective maintenance across electrical, vacuum, mechanical, plasma, hydraulic, and gas systems.
  • Lead and coordinate technical activities during equipment install, startup, qualification, and ramp phases.
  • Train, coach, and mentor junior Customer Engineers, helping to build technical capability across the team.
  • Build strong customer relationships through effective communication, responsiveness, and service delivery.
  • Identify opportunities for continuous improvement and share best practices to drive operational excellence.
  • Ensure all activities are performed in accordance with Applied Materials' safety, quality, and environmental standards.
  • Fulfil additional duties and project assignments as required.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Associate Degree, military technical training, trade certification, or equivalent technical experience.
  • 4-7 years of experience within the semiconductor industry or a related capital equipment, advanced manufacturing, or equipment support environment.
  • Strong mechanical and technical aptitude with experience in pneumatics, hydraulics, vacuum systems, electronics, thermodynamics, or related technologies.
  • Demonstrated troubleshooting and problem-solving experience within a customer-focused technical environment.
  • Experience working with hand tools, diagnostic equipment, and digital multimeters.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work directly with customers and cross-functional teams.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
  • Valid driver's licence and ability to obtain a passport if business travel is required.
  • Ability to meet all site-specific requirements, including safety, environmental, and customer compliance standards.

Why Join Applied Materials?

  • Support the technologies that enable the world's most advanced semiconductor manufacturing.
  • Work directly with leading semiconductor customers in highly complex, technology-driven environments.
  • Develop deep technical expertise across market-leading equipment platforms.
  • Access broad career opportunities spanning technical specialist, installation and ramp, product support, operations, and leadership pathways.
  • Learn from world-class engineers and benefit from continuous training and development.
  • Be part of a collaborative culture focused on innovation, customer success, and continuous improvement.

Physical Requirements:
This position often requires extensive walking, standing for extended periods of time, working in tight spaces, bending, squatting, twisting, kneeling, reaching, climbing stairs and ladders, working at height, lifting up to 35 lbs., the ability to distinguish between colors and working with electricity, the ability to work in an environment with noise that may be difficult for some individuals with sensitivity to noise, and the use of hand and power tools. Additionally, because this position generally involves working in a clean room, it requires the use of appropriate Personal Protective Equipment such as coveralls, hoods, booties, safety glasses, gloves, respirators, chemical aprons, and face shields.

Additional Information

Full time

Employee Type:

Assignee / Regular

Yes, 10% of the Time

Relocation Eligible:

No

title: Animal Care Specialist - Pell City - Part-Time
location: Pell City, Pell City, AL, US
description:
Animal Care Specialist

POSITION SUMMARY

The Greater Birmingham Humane Society (“the GBHS”) is a progressive animal welfare shelter whose mission is to rescue, rehabilitate, and rehome homeless, abused, neglected and abandoned animals. We are committed to an open admissions policy, animal rehabilitation and a low euthanasia rate. GBHS’ open intake and adoption philosophy is a key part of our progressive mission, enabling us to save and rehome thousands of animals each year.

The Animal Care Specialist will be responsible for providing and ensuring proper care to dogs, cats, and other animals at the shelter.

PRIMARY RELATIONSHIPS

  • Reports to Shelter Management and serves as a member of the animal care team.

  • Interacts daily with veterinarians, licensed veterinary technicians, foster coordinator, transport coordinator, volunteers, the general public, and potential adopters.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Performs cleaning details as directed by immediate supervisor and animal welfare standards
  • Responsible for feeding, cleaning, and the treatment of animals including but not limited to walking, bathing, exercise, and behavior.
  • Assists with the loading and unloading of animals with the transport driver
  • Assists in cleaning, sanitizing, and storing of crates and equipment
  • Works compassionately with injured and mistreated animals
  • Ensures the comfort and cleanliness of all animals on the adoption floor
  • Ensures animal areas are clean and orderly and stocked with food, litter, newspaper and other essential items
  • Understands basic animal infectious disease and willingness to prevent contagious spread
  • Documents behavior observations as needed and report them to manager
  • Documents medical observations immediately
  • Responsible for maintaining up to date identification cards and neck bands for all animals
  • Assists in maintaining overall facility cleaning standards
  • Assists with laundry tasks and general cleaning maintenance on a daily basis
  • Assists in enrichment and behavior as directed and show compassionate when working with all animals
  • Works collaboratively and communicates effectively with other members of the adoption team, as well as with other staff
  • Attends staff meetings and provide constructive feedback
  • Maintains personal appearance and uniform so as to appear professional at all times
  • Works closely with GBHS Volunteers in conjunction with the GBHS mission
  • Observes and follow strict nutrition and medical guidelines per veterinarian as directed
  • Provides excellent customer service to internal and external stakeholders
  • Provides general information to visiting patrons. For ex. Donors, school tours, general public
  • Performs such other duties as required by Manager
  • Follows all GBHS policies and protocols
  • Performs other duties as assigned

QUALIFICATIONS

  • A passion for the mission of GBHS and a sense of humor are required
  • High school diploma or GED equivalent
  • Must have reliable transportation to and from work, punctual attendance is required
  • Experience working with animals in veterinary, boarding, or a shelter environment preferred
  • Knowledge of animal handling and communication preferred
  • Working weekends may be required
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
  • Ability to work well in a team environment including a positive attitude and ability to get along with others

Education Requirements

Minimum of high school education or GED equivalent; customer service experience and a basic understanding of animal welfare; intermediate computer skills; meets minimum general requirements for GBHS employment as set forth in GBHS employee handbook.

Physical Requirements

Ability to perform physical work involving standing for long periods, carrying animal crates, bending, scrubbing, mopping, walking quickly, reaching, squatting and other such assigned duties with ease and in a timely fashion. Ability to lift and carry a minimum of 50 pounds or up to 75lbs with reasonable accommodation; ability to work weekends and evenings as necessary; meets minimum general requirements for GBHS employment as set forth in GBHS employee handbook.

Work Environment

This work is performed in a high noise level area. Exposure to industrial cleaning chemicals, fumes, dust, animal feces, zoonotic (human to animal) diseases, bites and scratches. Weekend shifts may be required. Safety procedures must be adhered to at all times. Must be able to work with and around animals of all types (cats, dogs, rabbits, birds, etc.). Exposure to conditions such as animal feces, urine, etc. and foul odors. May be exposed to animal dander, parasites and infectious diseases than can be carried and transmitted by animals. Must be able to work in an environment that provides humane euthanasia to animals.

The GBHS is an equal opportunity employer. It is the policy of GBHS to provide EEO to all persons regardless of age, color, national origin, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, race, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, genetic information, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law.


Must have availability on weekends.

description:

We are seeking a Senior Business Intelligence Engineer to take ownership of a company's data environment from end to end. This is a highly technical role combining Data Engineering, Business Intelligence, data visualization, automation, and AI enablement.

What You'll Do:

  • Own and maintain data pipelines and GCP infrastructure.

  • Develop and maintain Python-based ETL processes.
  • Build data pipelines and integrate new data sources into the data warehouse.
  • Automate recurring workflows and processes.
  • Monitor, troubleshoot, and improve pipeline performance and reliability.

Business Intelligence & Analytics

  • Build Tableau dashboards from the ground up.

AI & Automation

  • Look for opportunities to reduce manual coding and repetitive processes through intelligent automation.

Why Join This Team

This is an opportunity to own a critical function rather than simply contribute to one. You'll have meaningful ownership over how data is collected, structured, automated, visualized, and ultimately used across the organization.

Your work will directly influence how teams operate and make decisions, while giving you the opportunity to shape the future of the company's data environment through cloud technology, automation, AI, and business intelligence.

You'll work across teams, have real visibility into the impact of your work, and become the technical owner helping turn data into a true business asset.
