title: ENGINEER
description:
Job Description & Requirements

An electrical engineer designs, develops, tests, and maintains electrical systems and equipment that power nearly everything in modern life. From the smartphone in your pocket to the power grid lighting your city, electrical engineers are the problem-solvers who make complex electrical systems work safely and efficiently.

These professionals apply principles of electricity, electronics, and electromagnetism to create solutions across diverse industries. You’ll find them designing control systems for manufacturing plants, developing renewable energy infrastructure, creating navigation systems for aircraft, or testing components for medical devices.

The role goes far beyond just understanding circuits. Electrical engineers must analyze system requirements, perform detailed calculations, create technical drawings, ensure compliance with safety codes, and often supervise installation and testing. They’re equally comfortable with CAD software and oscilloscopes, budget spreadsheets and power distribution diagrams.

title: Software Development Engineer IV - Algorithms and Scientific Data
description:
Software Development Engineer IV - Algorithms and Scientific Data





Job Locations

US-CA-Santa Barbara | US-Remote






ID

2026-19658



Job Function

Engineering and R&D



Base Min

USD $107,100.00/Yr.



Base Max

USD $190,000.00/Yr.






































Overview









Bruker is enabling scientists to make breakthrough discoveries and develop new applications that improve the quality of human life. Bruker's high-performance scientific instruments and high-value analytical and diagnostic solutions enable scientists to explore life and materials at molecular, cellular, and microscopic levels. In close cooperation with our customers, Bruker is enabling innovation, improved productivity and customer success in life science molecular research, in applied and pharma applications, in microscopy and nanoanalysis, and in industrial applications, as well as in cell biology, preclinical imaging, clinical phenomics and proteomics research and clinical microbiology.


Today, worldwide more than 11,000 employees are working on this permanent challenge at over 90 locations on all continents. Bruker continues to build upon its extensive range of products and solutions, its broad base of installed systems and a strong reputation among its customers. Being one of the world's leading analytical instrumentation companies, Bruker is strongly committed to further fully meeting its customers' needs as well as continuing to develop state-of-the-art technologies and innovative solutions for today's analytical questions.

The Bruker NANO group is seeking a Staff SW Engineer for Windows Instrumentation and Automation. The Senior Software Engineer will provide programming design and development for Bruker's world leading nano-scale Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) product lines. You will work with other software developers, engineers, and scientists supporting and advancing the state-of-the art nanoscale systems technology by developing software from application design to hardware control. This position requires initiative, innovation, and responsibility working within a cooperative team environment to support existing and realize new customer products.

Location and Work Model

Santa Barbara, California, or fully remote. Remote employees must be able to collaborate effectively with a Santa Barbara-based team with no more than a three-hour time difference. Remote employees may be asked to travel to Santa Barbara up to two times per year.

Position Summary

Join the team building software for the world's most capable automated atomic force microscopes used in leading semiconductor fabs. Our systems generate rich scientific data at nanometer scales, and our software transforms that data into accurate, actionable measurements while coordinating sophisticated precision hardware.

We are seeking a hands-on Staff Software Engineer to lead the design, implementation, validation, and productization of algorithms for scientific data analysis. The role emphasizes signal and image processing, numerical analysis, and applied machine learning while remaining grounded in production Windows software, modern C++, C#/.NET/WPF, and instrument integration. You will own important technical decisions, guide cross-functional problem solving, and write production code that ships with our instruments.

This is a scientific algorithms, Windows desktop, and instrumentation software position. It is not a web, mobile, data-platform, or cloud application development role. Candidates whose experience is primarily web application development or cloud data engineering will not meet the core requirements.

Agentic software development is part of how our team engineers software, not an occasional productivity aid. We use GitHub Copilot Business with leading AI models throughout algorithm exploration, design, implementation, testing, debugging, refactoring, and review. The successful candidate will bring meaningful production experience with AI coding agents and will be expected to use and advance these workflows responsibly.















Responsibilities









- Design, implement, validate, optimize, and deploy algorithms that turn AFM, image, sensor, and metrology data into robust measurements and insights.
- Develop production algorithm and application software using modern C++/STL, C#, .NET, WPF, and Python where appropriate.
- Apply signal processing, image processing, numerical methods, statistical analysis, pattern recognition, and machine learning to challenging real-world measurement problems.
- Translate research concepts and prototypes into maintainable, testable, high-performance product software with clear requirements and measurable performance.
- Build validation strategies using representative datasets, quantitative metrics, uncertainty analysis, and regression tests; clearly communicate algorithm limits and tradeoffs.
- Integrate algorithms into multithreaded Windows applications and instrument workflows spanning data acquisition, hardware control, processing, persistence, visualization, and automation.
- Own architecture for new analysis capabilities and guide their integration into a mature product codebase through sound interfaces, layering, refactoring, and incremental delivery.
- Lead technical investigations and collaborate with applications scientists, systems, hardware, test, and software engineers throughout the product development cycle.
- Remain deeply hands-on while providing technical direction and raising algorithm and software engineering quality across a small cross-functional team.
- Use VS Code and AI coding agents as core engineering tools across the software development lifecycle while applying rigorous technical and scientific judgment to all generated work.















Qualifications









- 5+ years of professional experience developing production software, scientific algorithms, or data-analysis systems.
- 3+ years of hands-on Windows application development using both C#/.NET/WPF and modern C++/STL.
- Strong foundation in at least two of the following: signal processing, image processing, numerical methods, statistical analysis, pattern recognition, computer vision, or machine learning.
- Demonstrated ability to implement algorithms in C++, C#, or Python and to move them from exploration into tested, maintainable production software.
- Experience defining quantitative validation methods and evaluating algorithm accuracy, robustness, performance, and failure modes using real-world data.
- Strong object-oriented design, API design, debugging, data-structure, and performance-optimization skills.
- Experience with multithreaded or asynchronous software and computationally intensive data processing.
- Demonstrated architecture ownership and technical leadership across algorithm, application, or product boundaries.
- Meaningful, regular use of GitHub Copilot or comparable AI coding agents on production software. Candidates should be prepared to discuss specific examples spanning multiple development activities and how they ensure technical correctness and maintainability.
- Ability to collaborate clearly with engineers and scientists, communicate complex technical ideas and risks, and lead technical work without direct authority.

Education

- MS or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Data Science, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field is strongly preferred.
- A BS in a related field combined with significant relevant industry, instrumentation, algorithm-development, or research experience will be considered.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with scientific instrumentation, semiconductor metrology, atomic force microscopy, optical spectroscopy, robotics, machine vision, motion control, nano-positioning, or automated test equipment.
- Experience developing algorithms for noisy sensor data, microscopy images, surface measurements, anomaly detection, feature extraction, classification, segmentation, reconstruction, or calibration.
- Experience applying machine learning to physical measurements and working with limited, imbalanced, or imperfectly labeled scientific datasets.
- Knowledge of control systems, estimation, system identification, experimental design, or measurement uncertainty.
- Experience with C++/CLI, managed/native interoperability, MFC, or integrating Python-based research code with production C++ or .NET applications.
- Experience using architectural layering across hardware interfaces, acquisition, analysis, persistence, and desktop presentation layers.
- Experience with Scrum or another Agile development approach and a record of improving practical engineering processes.
- Experience making effective use of both VS Code and Visual Studio in a Windows development environment.

Physical and Environmental Requirements

- When working onsite, ability to lift and move equipment weighing up to 30 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.
- Ability and willingness to work periodically in a Class 1000 cleanroom using full gowning protocol and laboratory-appropriate attire. These requirements also apply to remote employees during onsite visits.

At Bruker, base salary is part of our total compensation. The estimated base salary range for this full-time position is between $107,100 and $190,000 and provides an opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within a role. The base salary for the role will depend on a several job-related factors, including, but not limited to education, training, experience, the geographic location of the successful candidate, skills, competencies, job-related knowledge and travel requirements for this position. Full-time employees may also be eligible for a performance-related incentive in addition to a full range of benefits including 401(k) with company match, an employee stock purchase plan, medical and dental plans, life insurance, short-term and long-term disability insurance, employee assistance program and paid time off including vacation, sick time and holidays, and more.

Bruker is an equal-opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics.

Certain positions at Bruker require compliance with export control laws and as a result, all interviewed candidates for all positions will be screened pre-interview to determine their eligibility in light of export control restrictions.

title: VP Finance, Global Business Services
description:
The Vice President, Global Business Services (GBS) leads a large, globally distributed organization across end-to-end service towers, centers of excellence, process excellence, data enablement, digital transformation, business insights, and regional delivery hubs. The model integrates ULS talent and strategic delivery partners to serve the enterprise at scale.

The Vice President, Global Business Services is the enterprise executive accountable for the strategy, operating model, performance, transformation, talent, controls, and sustained value delivery of GBS. The role has evolved well beyond traditional shared services leadership. It combines global operations, end-to-end process ownership, business partnership, digital and AI enablement, data and insights, and transformation.

The leader sets the aspiration for GBS and converts it into a sequenced portfolio of structural, operational, digital, and capability-building priorities. The role must simultaneously protect day-to-day service, improve customer outcomes, working capital and cost efficiency, modernize the footprint, and build scalable capabilities that position GBS as a trusted enterprise partner.

  • Enterprise strategy and operating model: Define and continuously evolve the GBS strategy, service portfolio, governance, delivery footprint, tower model, centers of excellence, and location strategy in alignment with enterprise and CFO priorities.
  • End-to-end accountability: Drive ownership across Order-to-cash, invoice-to-pay, payroll, customer care and certification operations, master data and data enablement, with clear process boundaries, service expectations, controls, and decision rights.
  • Operational performance: Lead a disciplined performance system anchored in SLAs, KPIs, quality, productivity, capacity, cost-to-serve, working capital, customer experience, risk, and control effectiveness. Intervene quickly where performance or business outcomes are at risk.
  • Transformation portfolio: Sponsor and govern a complex portfolio of operating-model, process, automation, AI, data, technology, and integration initiatives. Ensure investments have clear outcomes, owners, milestones, controls, adoption plans, and measurable benefits.
  • Digital, data and AI agenda: Build future-ready capabilities through intelligent automation, AI-enabled service delivery, governed data foundations, decision-focused insights, and thoughtful integration of technology into redesigned processes.
  • Business partnership: Serve as a senior advisor to the CFO, Finance Leadership Team, business segments, functions, and technology leaders. Translate enterprise needs into scalable solutions while challenging fragmented work, avoidable complexity, and local optimization.
  • Talent and culture: Build a diverse, high-performing global team; create succession depth and career pathways; strengthen site leadership and capability academies; and foster a culture of accountability, inclusion, continuous improvement, learning, and enterprise-first decision-making.
  • Risk, controls and compliance: Maintain a strong control environment across global operations, including SOX and financial reporting controls, audit readiness, data governance, third-party oversight, policy compliance, business continuity, and sustainable remediation.
  • Partner and commercial leadership: Own strategic service-provider relationships, statements of work, commercial protections, performance commitments, transition governance, quality assurance, and continuous value realization.
  • Enterprise change and integration: Lead sensitive global transformations, acquisitions, separations, transitions, and new-scope migrations with disciplined Day 1 readiness, stakeholder alignment, communications, talent planning, and stabilization.
  • 15+ years of progressive experience, including significant executive leadership of large-scale global operations, shared services or GBS, and enterprise transformation in a complex multinational environment.
  • Demonstrated success transforming a shared-services organization into an integrated GBS model with stronger end-to-end ownership, scalable delivery, measurable enterprise value, and disciplined governance.
  • Executive presence and credibility to advise, influence, and challenge C-suite leaders, business presidents, functional executives, boards, auditors, and external partners.
  • Proven ability to lead a broad portfolio spanning finance operations, customer operations, payroll, procurement operations, master data, process excellence, analytics, digital enablement, controls, and service management.
  • Strong commercial, financial, and operational acumen, including business cases, productivity and cost management, working capital, vendor contracts, investment prioritization, and benefit realization.
  • Practical understanding of digital transformation, automation, AI, enterprise platforms, data architecture, governance, and technology-enabled operating-model redesign.
  • Exceptional global people leadership, with experience building leadership teams, developing successors, leading through ambiguity, and inspiring geographically and culturally diverse organizations.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Business, Economics, Finance, Operations, Engineering, or a related discipline. Advanced degree preferred.

Pivotal Experience and Expertise:

  • GBS architect: Has designed and led a modern GBS model that integrates service delivery, process ownership, transformation, data, digital, controls, and talent under one enterprise agenda.
  • Transformation at scale: Has successfully led multi-year, cross-functional transformations involving organization redesign, process standardization, outsourcing or insourcing, location strategy, technology deployment, automation, and change management.
  • Operational rigor: Establishes transparent performance systems and has the judgment to distinguish isolated service issues from systemic process, capacity, accountability, or control failures.
  • Enterprise influence: Navigates matrixed organizations, aligns leaders with competing priorities, and moves decisions forward without relying solely on formal authority.
  • Digital and AI fluency: Connects emerging capabilities to real business problems, redesigns work before automating it, and balances speed with governance, control, adoption, and measurable impact.
  • Global footprint leadership: Has directed multi-country operations and delivery hubs, built resilient location and sourcing strategies, and managed strategic partners without diluting enterprise accountability.
  • Value orientation: Converts GBS performance into business outcomes, including customer experience, cash, growth enablement, productivity, cost, quality, control, cycle time, and organizational capacity.
  • Change leadership: Communicates with clarity and empathy, makes difficult decisions, builds followership, and leaves behind stronger leaders, capabilities, governance, and institutional discipline

Cultural Characteristics:

  • Enterprise-first and mission-driven: Puts the company, customers, and team ahead of functional ownership; connects GBS priorities to UL Solutions’ mission and enterprise strategy.
  • High standards, low ego: Raises the bar, invites challenge, gives credit broadly, and combines humility with the courage to make consequential decisions.
  • Customer and outcome obsessed: Looks beyond activity and technology deployment to the business result, end-to-end journey, and experience being created.
  • Accountable, metrics-driven, and decisive: Creates clarity, confronts issues directly, follows through, and expects leaders to own both performance and root-cause resolution.
  • Strategic and pragmatic: Holds the long-term vision while sequencing change realistically, protecting service continuity, and adapting as facts evolve.
  • Talent-centric and inclusive: Builds trust across cultures, develops people through expanded ownership, and creates opportunities for leaders and teams to grow with the operating model.
  • Curious and future-ready: Continuously benchmarks, learns, tests assumptions, and advances digital, data, AI, and process capabilities with disciplined judgment.
  • Connected collaborator: Builds durable partnerships across Finance, Technology, HR, Sourcing, Sales, operations, and the business to solve enterprise problems rather than shift them.

Total Rewards

We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. The estimated salary range for this position is $250,000 - $300,000 and is based on multiple factors, including job-related knowledge/skills, experience, geographical location, as well as other factors. This position is eligible for annual bonus compensation with a target payout of 40% of base salary and a 50% RSU and PSU grant. This position also provides health benefits such as medical, dental and vision; wellness benefits such as mental and financial health; and retirement savings (401K) commensurate with the standard rewards offered in each individual location or country. We also provide full-time employees with paid time off including vacation (25 days), holiday including floating holidays (12 days) and sick time off (72 hours).

title: Senior Backend & AI Engineer (Cyber-Engineering)
description:
About Stoïk

Founded in 2021, Stoïk aims at becoming the most relevant cyber company in Europe through:

  • An insurance product to reimburse clients in case of a cyber attack;

  • An internalized incident response team (CERT) to minimize the financial consequences of a cyber attack;

  • Top-notch prevention tools to reduce the likelihood of such an attack.

We sell only through intermediaries (brokers or MSPs) and now have an extensive partner network we keep solidifying. A few numbers so it gets more concrete:

  • We are 170+ people with a 40+ tech team.

  • We insure 14k+ companies across 7 markets in Europe, with turnovers ranging from €0 to €1B.

  • Our CERT is 30 people and handles 150+ incidents every month (from small compromise to full-scale ransomware attacks).

  • Our insurance product reimburses €15m+ annually.

In the next five years, we intend to take a leading role in protecting European companies against an increasing cyber risk. As a consequence, we aim at taking a significant share of the European cybersecurity software market.

Why build here

AI impacts us in two ways: (1) cyber risk is changing very fast on the attack side; and (2) many cyber problems that used to be super hard are now within reach. This makes it very interesting to build here:

  1. We are one of the only players in the world with a clear view on how cyber risk is changing. We literally reimburse clients for the financial consequences of attacks, so we know very well what types of attack cost money, what the trends are, and how hackers are updating their operations. We are able to cut through the noise and assess which products are worth building to reduce cyber risk efficiently. The noise is increasing as the innovation pace goes through the roof, so this is becoming one of our most precious assets.

  2. We have skin in the game and a perfect alignment of interests with our clients. If our prevention tools don't work, we pay more, because we insure our clients. That forces us to hold very high standards about what we build and the team building it. And to keep up with frontier cyber capabilities.

  3. Many problems have become simpler (but not simple!) because of AI. Think for instance of edge cases in detection that were very time-consuming but can now be handled decently well with well-set-up agents. We have no attachment to any single product, because we aim at solving cyber risk as a whole. If tomorrow one of our products becomes irrelevant because cyber risk has changed, we will drop it. On the contrary, that means we are currently super ambitious about what we can build, because we can help our clients in a coherent way.

As of now, we have built:

  • Tools to monitor vulnerabilities and misconfigurations in the IT system (EASM tool, phishing campaigns, AD scan, cloud scans).

  • Managed Services both on endpoints (the endpoint agent being a 3rd-party solution like CrowdStrike or SentinelOne) and on emails (fraud detection, mailbox compromise).

  • An Incident Management System (IMS) to automate a significant part of the CERT workload (forensics, communications, action plans).

This is quite balanced. Some of those require handling scale (Email Security processes 10m+ emails/day), others crafting smart workflows (IMS is about agent orchestration, testing them and making sure they are reliable on a critical task).

The role

We’re hiring for two distinct positions: an engineer to extend our AI-powered workflows in Python, and an experienced endpoint engineer to build our Go agent.

1) IMS - Extending the tool to every run team (Python). Our Incident Management System already automates a large part of the CERT workload. We're now extending its scope to:

  1. more complex incidents like full-scale ransomware, and

  2. all our run teams (underwriting, CSM, sales call prep).

The key quality here is the ability to ramp up fast and to deploy agentic capabilities solving the issue: understand a new team's workflow, ship something useful, and iterate. For ransomware response for instance, that means working directly with incident responders to understand their workflows and forensic tasks. You’ll build the tools, agent orchestration, and evaluation framework, and own the system’s reliability and adoption across our ransomware cases.

2) Endpoint Agent - Software inventory and risk detection (Go). You'll build an endpoint agent, in Go, that collects the software deployed on a machine and flags potential risks. This is a hard and critical problem: footprint, reliability, cross-platform behavior, and running quietly on someone else's production machines. Because of that, we're looking for someone with a strong previous experience in endpoint agent deployment and architecture.

We are iterating quite fast and have new projects frequently. So if your profile matches what's below, but that you're interested in another tool we've built, please reach out anyway.

Your profile

  • Strong engineering profile. Very smart, lots of agency, sense of urgency. Based in Paris.

  • You keep up with innovation and ruthlessly update your way of working. You're looking for a fast-paced and ambitious environment where you can grow and take ownership.

  • Previous senior+ backend experience. Notably you have 4+ years of experience running a production environment and handling speed-vs-reliability trade-offs.

  • Decent knowledge of cyber, or very curious about it.

  • Stack:

    • Go / Python (strong in at least one)

    • PostgreSQL

    • AWS / Terraform / K8s

Compensation

Competitive salary set to reflect the impact you'll have. We discuss salary and equity during the first screening call, before any technical assessment.

Process

  • Screening call - 30mn

  • Technical test - take home + 2h on-site debrief and live test

  • Fit round - 2h on-site with founders and future colleagues

  • Fully own the operational and tactical localization lifecycle for assigned titles, serving as the single point of accountability from kickoff through global launch.

  • Overseeing all language assets—including dubbing, subtitling, SDH, audio description, marketing supplementals, metadata, main/episodic titles, and forced narratives—proactively managing cross-functional expectations, timelines, budgets, quality control, and ensuring the launch readiness of localized assets for both long form and trailers.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Collaboration

  • Facilitate collaboration between Netflix, localization partners, and Language Producers to align timelines, deliverables, and quality standards. Oversee progress, resolve operational challenges, and ensure consistent, authentic localization that meets regional objectives.

Project & Workflow Management

  • Plan, schedule, and manage localization workflows for each assigned title, including setting the language suite strategy and vendor selection, bid management, financial tracking, and asset delivery.

  • Oversee context gathering, complexity assessment, source material distribution, and project tracking while maintaining operational efficiency, ensuring our localization partners are set up to create localized assets that meet the Netflix creative standard.

  • Analyze localization metrics and project data to identify opportunities for workflow optimization and to proactively resolve operational challenges.

  • Analyze title level localization metrics and data to identify opportunities for workflow optimization and to proactively resolve operational challenges.

Innovation & Continuous Improvement

  • Identify and flag challenges within the current workflow to support ongoing operational improvement.

  • Foster a culture of partnership, transparency, and continuous improvement within the team and with external partners.

Requirements

  • Flexibility to support cross-vertical needs outside of Scripted Series as they arise, at the discretion of the Content Localization Manager/Director.

  • 5-7 or more years of experience in localization in a high-demand, fast-paced environment, ideally in the entertainment industry; experience managing large-scale, cross-functional projects in a fast-paced environment.

  • Experience managing high-volume content pipelines, day and date workflows, and/or emerging content formats.

  • Strong systems-thinking and strategic problem-solving skills

  • Ability to handle a fast-paced environment, supervising several projects at various points of production (from development through delivery).

  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills; able to work effectively in collaboration with creative, operational, technical and product teams.

  • Make sound independent decisions, and know when to escalate issues

  • Highly analytical, data-driven, and solutions-oriented; able to identify root causes, optimize processes, and drive operational excellence.

  • Adaptable and resilient in the face of change and ambiguity; comfortable with evolving priorities, formats, experimentation and new challenges.

  • Passion for operational efficiency, localization or project management.

title: Quality Supervisor - 1st Shift
description:
We Create Products and Brands That People Trust to Clean, Sanitize, and Protect Their Homes and Pools

When you join KIK Consumer Products, you’re joining a team that cares about the work we do and also about each other. We bring exceptional brands and products to consumers that help them protect the health and wellness of their families and the cleanliness of their homes and pools. We are committed to building a culture of performance driven by accountability, collaboration, and agility that enables timely fact-based decision-making and exceptional execution with unwavering ethics. As one of North America’s largest independent manufacturers of consumer products, KIK helps a large portfolio of brands and retailers bring their products to life.

Your Role at KIK

As the Quality Supervisor on 1st Shift (6:00am - 4:30pm, Monday-Thursday with weekends per business need) you are responsible for overseeing quality control processes on the production floor to ensure that products meet company standards and regulatory requirements. This role leads a team of quality technicians and inspectors, coordinates daily quality activities, investigates non-conformances, and collaborates with production and engineering teams to drive continuous improvement. The Quality Supervisor ensures that quality procedures are followed, documentation is accurate, and corrective actions are effectively implemented. This position plays a key role in maintaining product integrity, minimizing defects, and supporting customer satisfaction through strong quality oversight.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Review of production line and performance for adherence to company Standard Operating Procedures, Quality Guidelines, and facility procedures.
  • Responsible for auditing documentation of testing, holding products, internal investigations, and root cause analysis.
  • Oversees quality functions regarding development and maintenance of product specifications.
  • Develops/monitors training systems and programs supporting a total quality organization.
  • Control and reporting monthly quality data
  • Control and reporting of store retail check data
  • Reviews/Monitors production deviations related to Quality
  • Actively lead by example the quality culture we aspire to working as a team with all plant personnel

The above statement describes the general nature and level off work only. They are not an exhaustive list of all required responsibilities, duties, and skills. Other duties may be added, or this description amended at any time.

What You’ll Bring

  • Associate's degree or equivalent industry certifications; Bachelor's degree preferred
  • 3 years’ experience preferred in filling/packaging manufacturing environment
  • Excellent mathematic and problem-solving skills
  • Familiar with using: Refract meter, viscometer, pH meter, digital titrators and an analytical balance
  • Understand mechanical aptitude plus be able to do wet chemistry-titrations, pH adjustment, and acid/base dilution.
  • Knowledge of Quality systems and applications are required.
  • Ability to drive organizational change
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills
  • Highly motivated individual looking to advance in this career

What You Will Get

KIK offers a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits including health, wellness, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance. You can plan for your future with KIK's retirement savings options including employer match. KIK also recognizes the importance of continuing education and offers Education Assistance to our employees to encourage continued personal development and growth.

We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. This position has a base salary of $70,000-$75,000 plus an annual incentive bonus. The actual salary may vary based upon several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant skills/experience, time in the role, business line, and geographic/office location.

About KIK

We create the products and brands that people trust to clean, sanitize, and protect their homes and pools. We are one of North America’s largest independent consumer product manufacturers with 16 North American manufacturing facilities. We also operate globally in Canada, Europe, and Australia. We are known for our portfolio of notable brands including Spic and Span® and Comet® cleaning products, Clorox® Pool&Spa™ (under license), BioGuard®, and Natural Chemistry® pool chemicals. We are also the #1 producer in North America of store-brand (“private label”) bleach and a leading private-label provider of laundry detergent and additives, dishwashing products, general-purpose cleaning, and other home care products.

Our global team of over 2,300 employees drives our capabilities in product development, product formulation, strategic sourcing, manufacturing, packaging design, brand marketing, project management, quality assurance, compliance, distribution, and logistics.

Our organization is constantly evolving and is driven by a set of “One KIK” values – a dedication to following through on commitments in a customer-focused, profit-motivated way; while never compromising on safety, ethics, or integrity.

title: Quality Engineering Technician- 2nd Shift
description:
Join a Team That Makes a Difference!

At Noble, the work you do matters. We manufacture innovative products that support the military, advance the medical field, and improve everyday life. Whether it's enhancing safety, enabling critical care, or solving real-world challenges, our solutions help people when it matters most. Be part of a purpose-driven team where your skills contribute to meaningful change.

Noble Biomaterials, Inc is currently seeking a Quality Engineering Technician on our 2nd shift (2pm-10pm). The Quality Engineering Technician (QA Technician) is a hands-on, manufacturing-focused quality role that provides real-time support to daily production operations. This position is embedded on the production floor and partners closely with Fabric Operations, Process Engineering, and Production to reinforce quality procedures, support inspection and disposition decisions, and ensure accurate and compliant documentation. This role is critical to supporting the expansion to two-shift fabric manufacturing and serves as the primary quality presence on the production floor during second shift. This is not a laboratory role—the focus is on manufacturing execution, quality discipline, and operational decision-making.


What You’ll Do:

  • Serve as the primary Quality Assurance representative on the production floor during second shift.
  • Support fabric inspection activities, including visual inspections, in-process checks, and disposition decisions in accordance with approved procedures and specifications.
  • Partner with the Fabric Quality Engineer, QE Manager, Operations, and Process Engineering on day-to-day quality decisions.
  • Reinforce adherence to approved work instructions, control plans, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
  • Monitor quality performance trends and assist with root cause analysis and failure investigations.
  • Utilize quality tools (InfinityQS, JMP, Decision Logs) to analyze performance trends and document deviations.

Documentation & Good Documentation Practices (GDP)

  • Ensure accurate, complete, and timely completion of batch records, travelers, inspection records, and manufacturing documentation in compliance with GDP requirements.
  • Review documentation for accuracy, completeness, and compliance prior to escalation or release.
  • Verify that process documentation reflects current manufacturing practices and escalate discrepancies as needed.

Operational & Cross-Functional Support

  • Support Operations and Process Engineering with real-time issue identification, containment actions, and production floor feedback.
  • Assist with the implementation and reinforcement of approved process changes and procedural updates.
  • Act as a quality liaison between shifts to ensure continuity of communication, issues, and corrective actions.

Continuous Improvement & Compliance

  • Identify quality risks, recurring issues, and gaps in procedural adherence; escalate appropriately.
  • Support internal audits, inspections, and quality initiatives.
  • Promote a strong quality culture through visibility, clear communication, and consistent expectations.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Perform other related duties as assigned by Quality or Operations management.

The Skills You'll Need:

  • Basic computer skills required (Microsoft Office, electronic forms, data entry).
  • Familiarity with manufacturing documentation systems, GDP, and ISO 9001 concepts is a plus.
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to identify procedural or documentation discrepancies.
  • Ability to make practical, well-reasoned decisions within established quality frameworks.
  • Comfortable working on the manufacturing floor for extended periods.
  • Able to follow procedures precisely while recognizing when escalation is required.
  • Self-motivated and capable of working independently during off-shift hours.
  • Quick learner with the ability to absorb technical and procedural information.
  • Strong sense of ownership, accountability, and follow-through.
  • Effective communicator across Quality, Operations, and Engineering teams.


What We’re Looking For:

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Previous experience in a manufacturing or quality environment strongly preferred.
  • Experience as a production lead, senior operator, or quality technician is highly desirable.
  • Quality control experience preferred; laboratory experience is not required and is not the focus of this role.
  • Ability to train 12pm-8pm until training is completed

title: Clinical Program Director: School-Based K-12
description:
CLINICAL PROGRAM DIRECTOR

Location

NuView Academy, Piscataway NJ

Setting

State-run therapeutic day school: a self-contained program for K-12 students with the highest level of emotional, behavioral, and mental health needs

Schedule

Full-time, 12-month schedule (academic/clinical calendar runs through summer, with school breaks off plus two weeks in August). Monday–Friday, primarily daytime, with one evening per week for coverage and a monthly evening parent support group. No weekends.

Reports To

Clinical Regional Director

Salary Range

$90,000–$95,000, commensurate with experience and licensure

About the Role

Effective School Solutions (ESS) is a well-established, rapidly growing organization changing the nature of in-school mental health services for K-12 students.

The Clinical Program Director leads the clinical and operational success of ESS's program at NuView Academy, supporting K-12 students with the highest level of need — many of whom are stepping down from hospitalization or residential care, or could not be safely maintained in a traditional public school. This is a high-responsibility, high-impact role: you'll provide leadership to clinical staff, own program operations, and serve as the primary point of contact between ESS and school leadership, all while making sure some of the highest-need students in the state get the intensive care they need to stabilize and move forward.

This role is built for a seasoned, independently licensed clinician who is ready to lead at a program level. It's a fast-paced environment where priorities shift quickly, so comfort anticipating needs before they're voiced and making sound decisions with incomplete information goes a long way. You bring deep clinical expertise with acute, high-need student populations, real experience managing and developing clinical leaders and teams, and the relationship-building skills to earn trust with school and state education leadership alike. In return, you'll get a structured, well-resourced program to run, a team of experienced clinical and educational leaders behind you, and the kind of ownership that comes with building something that works, plus extensive training in ESS protocols, systems, and service models as you get started.

What You'll Do

Clinical Leadership

  • Provide weekly individual clinical supervision (~9 hours/week) to Clinicians and Mental Health Technicians, including consultation and oversight for individual, group, and family interventions.
  • Lead weekly consultation meetings on treatment planning, progress monitoring, and documentation compliance.
  • Represent ESS in IEP meetings, manifestation determinations, disciplinary hearings, and re-entry planning following hospitalization or disciplinary action.
  • Coordinate care across families, school staff, psychiatrists, and community providers so students move smoothly across the full continuum of care.
  • Collaborate directly with the psychiatrist on medication management — appointment setting, confirmation, and follow-through with families and the school nurse — acting as the bridge between psychiatry and the school.
  • Build strong multidisciplinary partnerships that support students' academic, behavioral, and emotional success.
  • Lead family engagement efforts, including a monthly in-person parent support group, parent meetings, and educational programming.
  • Serve as the program's go-to expert for managing crises and high-risk student situations and be available by phone to support staff providing after-hours family therapy.

Program & Operational Leadership

  • Own day-to-day program operations and people management for the clinical team — staffing, scheduling, adherence to ESS standards, performance feedback, annual reviews, and corrective action, in partnership with the Clinical Regional Director and HR.
  • Partner with ESS's Regional Recruiting Manager on interviewing and hiring clinical staff.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact with school and district leadership on program needs, outcomes, and student support, and report program progress to district and ESS leadership.
  • Identify potential clinical, relationship, or staffing issues early, and resolve them independently and effectively.
  • Coordinate with school leaders on tours, referrals, and assessment scheduling for prospective students and families.
  • Step in to cover clinical coverage gaps when needed.
  • Ensure clinical documentation is accurate, timely, and compliant with ESS, ethical, and regulatory standards.
  • Track and analyze program data (attendance, behavior, academics, utilization) and turn it into action plans that close performance gaps.
  • Represent ESS professionally across the district, traveling as needed to support your team.

What You Bring

Required

  • Master's degree in Social Work, Counseling, Marriage and Family Therapy, or a related mental health field.
  • Active, independent clinical license (LCSW, LPC, LMFT) in NJ.
  • Certification to provide clinical supervision.
  • 6–8 years providing clinical services to children and adolescents with significant behavioral, emotional, or mental health challenges.
  • 3–5 years of supervisory or leadership experience in a clinical setting.
  • Proven ability to build trust and strong working relationships with school administrators, district leaders, families, and community partners.
  • Strong leadership, communication, organizational, and project management skills, with a solution-focused approach to problem solving.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and electronic documentation/EHR systems.

Preferred

  • Prior experience in a school-based mental health program.
  • Experience supervising multidisciplinary teams.
  • Comfort using data to drive clinical and operational decisions.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary Range: $90,000–$95,000, based on experience and licensure.
  • Health, dental, and vision coverage.
  • 401K plan with employer match.
  • Company-paid life insurance and disability coverage.
  • PTO and paid holidays.
  • Access to CEUs and professional development.
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP), plus access to discount programs for entertainment/travel and a childcare network.

Why Join Effective School Solutions?

  • Be part of a mission-driven organization addressing the growing mental health needs of children and adolescents.
  • Work alongside experienced clinical and educational leaders dedicated to improving student outcomes.
  • Step into a real leadership track: this role is a launchpad toward regional and multi-site clinical leadership opportunities.
  • Contribute your expertise to an organization that values clinician voice, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Equal Opportunity Employer

ESS is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment on the basis of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class.

title: Junior Front End Engineer
description:
Common Wealth exists to make retirement security accessible to all Canadians. As Canada’s fastest-growing group retirement provider, we serve over 1,700 employers across the country and are helping tens of thousands of Canadians build long-term financial security. Our award-winning retirement technology and services platform makes it easy for employers of all sizes to offer competitive retirement benefits, empowers members to build wealth with confidence, and equips advisors with tools to better serve their clients. We work closely with a rapidly expanding network of advisors, for whom we strive to be a true partner in powering the growth of their business.

About the role

We are looking for a Junior Front End Engineer to join Common Wealth’s engineering team. You will play a key role in contributing to building and scaling the technology that powers our retirement platform to help us drive toward a future where every Canadian can achieve financial security in retirement. Professional / personal exposure to fintech is a strong plus.

You’ll focus on the front end, building robust, scalable applications with React and TypeScript, deployed on our AWS infrastructure. Familiarity with full-stack work (Java/Kotlin/PostgreSQL back end) is a bonus. We value engineers who move fluidly across the stack and work closely with product and design.

What you will do:

  • Write, maintain and deliver code that delivers business objectives. You build product with a strong understanding of both client and business needs. You take pride in writing high quality, readable, and maintainable code. You’ll balance short-term speed with thoughtful investment in areas that are core to the platform.
  • Practice user-centric design. You will think critically about user experience and take into consideration accessibility and responsiveness.
  • Project delivery. Work within a talented cross‑functional team, collaborating closely with product and design. You will help shape technical requirements, brainstorm solutions, break down deliverables into milestones, and drive timelines to completion.

Who you are:

Note that you may not have touched our exact frameworks or tooling, and that's fine – we care more that you have a solid foundation and are able to learn fast than that you arrive knowing ours.

  • User focused. You’re passionate about solving our clients' problems together. You focus on delivering a smooth user experience that delights our users and proactively identify and propose solutions to UX problems.
  • Foundation as front end developer. You have previous experience through co‑op / internship or 1+ year full time experience in building frontend applications with React, TypeScript, and SASS. You are familiar with Redux, accessibility, and responsive design.
  • End-to-end mindset. You have background in building maintainable and testable code. Bonus if you have worked with Cypress and Storybook.
  • Comfortable with AI-assisted coding tools. You leverage AI tools as part of your normal workflow and understand their strengths and limitations. You review, test, and take ownership of AI-generated output.
  • Impact driven. Your work goes beyond the code you write. You seek to understand the business side and how the applications you build directly contribute to the success of the organization and excite our users.
  • Thrive in collaboration. You believe that great products are built through teamwork. You work closely with product and design teams, keeping an open channel for continuous feedback and collaboration that makes the product better.
  • Curious and self‑directed learner. You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity and are motivated to explore, learn, and grow. You stay on top of emerging tools that enhance your technical foundation.
  • Infrastructure on AWS: IaC with CDK, Docker, ECS, Fargate, RDS Aurora / PostgreSQL, S3, DynamoDB, CloudFront, Lambda@Edge, Cognito, GuardDuty
  • Other Tools: Datadog, LaunchDarkly, LogRocket

Why work with us:

title: Third Person in Charge
description:
Safeway has an opening for a Third Person in Charge!

The Third Person in Charge is responsible for the operations of the entire store when the Store Director (SD) and Assistant Store Director (ASD) are not present. The position is one of the job classifications from which candidates for retail leadership development training are typically selected, the successful completion of which may lead to advancement into store management. The Third Person in Charge provides customer service, administers training to new employees, coordinates with others to determine hiring needs and to identify and select candidates for interviews, and assists with merchandising execution for the store. The Third Person also coordinates with the late shift employees in directing the day-to-day activities of the late shift when the Store Director and Assistant Store Director are not present, including assessment of daily operational needs and training personnel. Assists in ordering, receiving storing, pricing, stocking and merchandising.

Responsibilities

  • Works primarily closing shifts to run total store operations in the absence of the Store Director and Assistant Store Director.
  • Works with the Assistant Store Director on center of store operations and fills in for Assistant Store Director on their days off, when the ASD is filling in for Store Director, or while the ASD is on vacation.
  • Overall management responsibility for the total store operation, including supervision of all employees and the handling of customer complaints, in the absence of the Store Director and Assistant Store Director.
  • Initiates corrective action as needed in the absence of the Store Director and Assistant Store Director.
  • Acts as the liaison between the Store Director/Assistant Store Director and the late shift operations to ensure smooth operations of the store.
  • Encourages and maintains an atmosphere of enthusiastic customer awareness with an emphasis on fast, friendly, courteous customer service. Engages in suggestive selling and other sales techniques. Handles customer relations issues.
  • Performs ordering, receiving, storing, pricing, stocking, and merchandising duties. Coordinates with late shift employees/department leads in planning, organizing, and directing day-to-day operations of the store during the late shift and special sales/AD needs. Assists with implementing Company and Division merchandising policies and/or Store Director instructions.
  • Coordinates with Assistant Store Director to prepare "things to do list" for night stockers for closing shifts; prepares "things to do list" for day stockers for day or mid shifts.
  • May perform duties of the receiving clerk in the absence of the Inventory Control Clerk.

Ensures all new hire paperwork and policies are acknowledged by all new hires and/or promoted employees and maintained in personnel files.

title: Project Controls Lead – Data Center Capital P
location: West Palm Beach, West Palm Beach, FL, US
description:
Position Overview

The Project Controls Lead is responsible for financial governance, scheduling fidelity, risk management, and change control of large-scale data center construction projects. Working in tight alignment with Project Directors and Project Managers, this role establishes the project baseline, continuously analyzes earned value, forecasts cash flows, and ensures that complex multi-megawatt builds deliver on budget and on schedule.

This is a data-driven, highly analytical advisory and governance role operating at the intersection of capital construction finance and critical infrastructure engineering.

Key Responsibilities

1. Baseline, Cost, & Schedule Control

· WBS/CBS Ownership: Establish, manage, and monitor the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) and Cost Breakdown Structure (CBS).

· Budget Management: Serve as the principal lead for budget management, precise cash flow forecasting, invoice reviews, monthly/quarterly accruals, and risk facilitation for a given datacenter site.

· Integrated Master Schedule (IMS): Collaborate with planning teams to maintain resource-loaded schedules (typically Level 1–4 in Primavera P6), ensuring critical path dependencies (such as utility power arrivals, long-lead equipment lead times, and structural handoffs) are accurate.

· EVM Metrics: Drive Project Percentage Completion (PPC) and Earned Value Management (EVM), tracking Schedule Variance (SV), Cost Variance (CV), and generating predictable Estimate at Completion (EAC) models.

2. Cash Flow, Long-Lead Equipment & OFCI Tracking

· Supply Chain Integration: Monitor the financial milestones, delivery schedules, and logistics for Owner-Furnished, Contractor-Installed (OFCI) infrastructure (e.g., MV/LV switchgear, major transformers, generators, and Chilled Water Systems/CDUs).

· Cash Flow Curves: Develop and maintain monthly cash flow curves and milestone payment schedules for major OEM vendors.


3. Change Management & Variance Analysis

· Rigorous Change Control: Manage and audit the project change log. Evaluate and approve the cost and schedule impacts of field change orders, requests for information (RFIs), and engineering design updates before approval.

· Root-Cause Forecasting: Identify early indicators of budget creep or schedule slippage. Conduct variance analysis and partner with construction managers to design actionable recovery plans.

4. Risk Mitigation & Commissioning Alignment

· Quantitative Risk Analysis: Facilitate risk workshops, update the project risk register, and utilize quantitative methods (such as Monte Carlo simulations) to maintain appropriate cost and schedule contingencies.

· Commissioning Continuity: Align cash flows and progress metrics with the distinct Level 1 through Level 5 (L1–L5) commissioning phases, ensuring accurate earned-value recognition through Integrated Systems Testing (IST) and final handover.

5. Executive Governance & Reporting

· Dashboards & KPIs: Design and automate real-time performance dashboards (using tools like Power BI or advanced Excel/Power Query) tracking Cost Performance Index (CPI) and Schedule Performance Index (SPI).

· Stakeholder Briefings: Compile transparent monthly project status reports and deliver data-driven briefings to internal executives, joint-venture partners, or hyper-scale tenants.

Required Technical Skills & Qualifications

· Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Finance, Data Analytics, or a heavily quantitative discipline.

· Experience: 10+ years of dedicated project controls or cost engineering experience on large capital projects ($200M+ value), with a minimum of 2 years directly within the mission-critical, high-performance computing, or data center sector, preferably General Contractor or contractor experience.

· Software Proficiency: * Advanced mastery of scheduling software (Primavera P6).

o Expertise in Microsoft Excel (data modeling, Power Query, advanced formulas).

o Experience with construction management platforms (e.g., Archdesk, Autodesk Construction Cloud).

o Familiarity with business intelligence tools (Power BI or Tableau) for building executive automated reporting is highly preferred.

· Domain Knowledge: Solid grasp of data center architecture, major mechanical/electrical/plumbing (MEP) layouts, and the sequential nature of critical infrastructure builds.

Core Competencies & Behavioral Traits

· Uncompromising Precision: Strong attention to detail; able to spot systemic forecasting trends or minor discrepancies within massive, multi-tiered spreadsheets and contractor billings.

· Cross-Functional Diplomat: Excellent communication and influence skills. Capable of translating complex financial and scheduling variances into clear, actionable advice for field superintendents, technical engineers, and senior executives alike.

· Thrives in Velocity: Adept at managing changing priorities and overlapping deadlines within the high-speed, high-stress environment of fast-tracked hyperscale or colocation developments.

title: Data Engineer
description:
We are hiring for Elastic Data Engineer – SIEM / Data Onboarding

Location: Multiple locations across the United Kingdom (UK)

We are looking for a hands-on Senior Elastic Data Engineer with strong Data Engineering skills, particularly in onboarding raw, unstructured and semi-structured log data into Elastic Security / SIEM.

This is primarily a data onboarding and pipeline engineering role we need someone who is comfortable taking an unfamiliar raw log source, understanding its structure, building the required parsing and transformation logic, mapping it to ECS, and taking the data feed through to production.

Key skills we’re looking for:

  • Strong experience onboarding unstructured, semi-structured and structured logs from security, network, infrastructure and application platforms
  • Hands-on development of Logstash pipelines for raw log ingestion and transformation
  • Strong experience with Elasticsearch ingest pipelines
  • Ability to parse complex and inconsistent log formats using Dissect, Grok, KV, JSON, CSV, scripting and native processors
  • Experience handling syslog (RFC 3164 / RFC 5424) and multiple event formats within the same data source
  • Strong understanding of Elastic Common Schema (ECS) and security data normalisation
  • Experience designing data streams, mappings, component templates, index templates and ILM policies
  • Hands-on experience with Elastic Agent, Fleet and integrations, including Custom Logs and Custom TCP/UDP
  • Experience with Kafka → Logstash → Elasticsearch ingestion architectures
  • Strong pipeline testing and troubleshooting skills, including malformed events, parsing failures and mapping conflicts
  • Ability to own the complete data onboarding lifecycle — discovery, source-to-target mapping, development, testing, QA, deployment, validation and handover

What’s particularly important

We are looking for someone with genuine data engineering and log onboarding experience, not just Elastic administration, Kibana dashboarding or SIEM rule configuration.

You should be comfortable being given a raw/unfamiliar log sample and independently working out how to parse, normalise, enrich and onboard it into Elastic in a scalable and maintainable way.

Desirable certifications:

Elastic Certified Engineer

Elastic Certified Analyst

If you have strong Elastic + Data Engineering + raw log onboarding experience, we’d be interested in speaking with you.

description:
Job Function Summary:

Under direct supervision of the Otolaryngology – (OHNS) Practice Supervisor, the Ambulatory Administrative Coordinator will work independently and have responsibility for providing administrative support to the Facial Plastic OHNS practice. The the Ambulatory Administrative Coordinator functions as primary contact for tertiary new and returning patients requiring ambulatory care at UCSF Health Facial Plastics. S/he will work closely with the administrative and management teams to support practice operations, complex surgery scheduling, billing and work queue knowledge and advanced care coordination with multiple departments at UCSF. The Ambulatory Administrative Coordinator serves as a liaison to management to advise on, take lead action on, and provide direction on process improvements initiatives. S/he provides support to all functions of the administrative teams including oversight of: registering and scheduling patients, checking in and out patients, referral work queue management, authorizations, insurance verification, surgery depot management, OR block time utilization, APeX in baskets, scanning and filing. As an Ambulatory Administrative Coordinator, s/he is responsible for addressing and resolving escalated issues of day to day operations in addition to maintaining daily administrative operations and communications relations to the clinic staff, to social workers, physicians and multiple department staff when coordinating advanced care. As a subject-matter expert in patient scheduling and the electronic medical record, the Ambulatory Administrative Coordinator will assist in template building, adjustments, scheduling improvements, and work with support staff and the clinical team to ensure seamless day-to-day clinic operations. The Ambulatory Administrative Coordinator will participate in performance improvement initiative such as the True North Board, in pulling data for the clinic and in feedback related to staff performance. The Ambulatory Administrative Coordinator will participate in UCSF’s Ambulatory-wide initiatives to represent the department and may also present at monthly staff meetings and division meetings with any updates.

S/he must have the ability to perform and prioritize multiple tasks and work well with staff, patients and providers. title: ANW Coördinator
description:
Zo werk jij

Voor wie jij er bent? Onze patiënten die tijdens de avond, nacht en in het weekend zorg nodig hebben. Jij zorgt voor continuïteit en kwaliteit van de geboden zorg en bewaak je het zorgproces buiten kantoortijden. Dit doe je samen met een dienstdoende arts. Tijdens je dienst ben jij het centrale aanspreekpunt voor de verpleegkundige en verzorgende teams. Je werkgebied bestaat uit de klinische afdelingen op het terrein Zon & Schild in Amersfoort. Samen met 40 collega's bedienen we onder nabij 240 patiënten, welke kort of langdurend op het terrein verblijven. Als ANW-coördinator houd jij het overzicht en ben je hun achterwacht. Je werkt zelfstandig en schakelt snel tussen uiteenlopende situaties. Soms is telefonisch advies voldoende, op andere momenten ga je zelf naar een afdeling. Bij complexe situaties en calamiteiten werk je nauw samen met de dienstdoende arts. Kortom, je bent er als coördinator ANW door:

  • triage te verrichten en tijdens je dienst het centrale aanspreekpunt te zijn;

  • telefonisch of op de afdeling zelfstandig (complexe) problemen op te lossen en waar nodig te overleggen met de dienstdoende arts;

  • crisissituaties te managen, roosterproblemen het hoofd te bieden en acute opnames mogelijk te maken;

  • verpleegkundige, psychiatrische en somatische problematiek te beoordelen en waar nodig passende actie te ondernemen;

  • structurele knelpunten te signaleren, bespreekbaar te maken en hierop te anticiperen;

  • de kwaliteit en continuïteit van de verpleegkundige zorg buiten kantoortijden te borgen;

  • verantwoordelijkheid te dragen voor personele en personeelgerelateerde zaken tijdens je dienst.

Je werkt in de avond, nacht, weekenden en op feestdagen volgens een rooster.

Jouw team

Hoe je het team ANW het beste kunt omschrijven? Betrokken, professioneel en zelfstandig. Je krijgt veel verantwoordelijkheid en ruimte om vanuit je deskundigheid beslissingen te nemen. Tegelijkertijd kun je terugvallen op de dienstdoende arts. En minstens zo belangrijk: we hebben plezier in wat we doen. We werken hard, mét ons hart.

Wij zorgen voor jou

Werk dat ertoe doet en waar je van betekenis bent, dat is alvast onze eerste belofte. Omdat we een grote organisatie zijn met verschillende werklocaties kunnen we inspelen op ontwikkelwensen en voorkeuren qua functie-inhoud, type behandelprogramma en woon-werkafstand. We zien wie je bent en wat je kan. Als coördinator ANW bij GGz Centraal kun je in ieder geval rekenen op:

  • een bruto maandsalaris volgens CAO GGZ, FWG 55 (tussen € 3.231,- en € 5.027,- o.b.v. 36 uur​). Bereken hier jouw netto salaris.

  • een contract voor maximaal 28 uur per week voor onbepaalde tijd. We werken vanuit vertrouwen, dus je krijgt meteen een vast contract.

  • een vakantietoeslag en een eindejaarsuitkering van 8,33%.

  • 166 verlofuren en 35 levensfase-uren o.b.v. 36 uur. Zo willen we bijdragen aan een goede werk-privébalans.

  • een jaarlijks balansbudget van €1.000,- naar rato. Dit budget kun je besteden aan iets waar jij blij van wordt. Denk aan een cursus, extra salaris of verlofuren, aan jou de keuze.

Boven alles bieden we je een uitdagende en afwisselende baan met de ruimte om jezelf professioneel en persoonlijk te ontwikkelen via opleidingen, trainingen en interne scholing.
Onze arbeidsvoorwaarden zijn conform de CAO GGZ. Heb je vragen? Laat het ons weten.

Dit breng je mee

Je hebt affiniteit met de verschillende doelgroepen binnen de psychiatrie. Omdat je tijdens een ANW-dienst veel zelfstandig werkt, kun je goed prioriteiten stellen, blijf je rustig onder druk en durf je beslissingen te nemen. Je denkt in oplossingen, houdt overzicht en weet wanneer je zelf handelt en wanneer je anderen moet inschakelen.

Je past binnen GGz Centraal als je vanuit jouw expertise wilt bijdragen aan de allerbeste zorg.

Ook heb je voor deze baan:

  • een achtergrond als verpleegkundige met hbo werk- en denkniveau, waarbij somatische kennis een pre is;

  • een bij je functie behorende BIG-registratie;

  • kennis van relevante wet- en regelgeving, waaronder de Wet verplichte ggz (Wvggz);

  • ruime ervaring als verpleegkundige en bij voorkeur ervaring als coördinator/ANW;

  • bij voorkeur ervaring binnen de ggz en/of acute psychiatrische zorg.

Wie zijn wij?

Elk jaar rekenen zo’n 25.000 patiënten op ons als de specialist in geestelijke gezondheidszorg in midden Nederland. Vanuit verschillende locaties, binnen de thuissetting én online, bieden we specialistische hulp aan mensen met psychische problemen, in alle fasen van hun leven. Ontdek meer over GGz Centraal als werkgever en over onze visie en missie.

Onze locaties vind je in het midden van het land. Ons werkgebied strekt zich uit over Eemland, Flevoland, Gooi & Vechtstreek en Veluwe & Veluwe Vallei. Jouw nieuwe werkplek? Zon & Schild ligt in een goed bereikbare en bosrijke omgeving aan de rand van Amersfoort. Wij bieden een breed behandelaanbod aan patiënten met sterk uiteenlopende ziektebeelden en zorgbehoeften. Wij bieden zowel acute als langdurige zorg, wij kennen open en gesloten afdelingen en afdelingen voor zowel volwassenenpsychiatrie als ouderenpsychiatrie.

De resultaatverantwoordelijke zorgeenheid Eemland ontfermt zich over een breed werkgebied. Regio Eemland is volop in ontwikkeling. De aandacht is gericht op doelmatige behandeling waarbij herstelgerichte transmurale patiëntenzorg in de keten centraal staat. Samenwerking, optimalisatie en innovatie vind je terug in de visie op patiëntenzorg én werkgeverschap.
De coördinatoren ANW maken deel uit van de acute zorg binnen Eemland waarin de Crisisdienst, acute klinische opname (HIC), IHT en acute deeltijd nauw samenwerken. Het team ANW valt onder de kliniek Medium care.

Solliciteren

Zet jouw talenten in als coördinator ANW en versterk GGz Centraal in Amersfoort. Wil je meer inhoudelijke informatie over de vacature? Bel of app dan met de teammanager Ingrid de Boer, teamleider, via 06-49805049. Voor overige vragen helpt de recruiter je graag verder op weg. Kom je graag eerst sfeer proeven? Een dagdeel meelopen is mogelijk als onderdeel van de sollicitatieprocedure. Als we dé geschikte kandidaat hebben gevonden, sluiten we de vacature. Hebben we onze match nog niet gevonden? Dan zoeken we nog wat langer door.

Kom je bij ons werken, dan checken we standaard referenties en vragen we je om een actuele Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag (VOG). Natuurlijk vergoeden wij deze kosten. Een assessment kan onderdeel zijn van de sollicitatieprocedure.

title: Fullstack Developer
description:
Fullstack Engineer – Fletchers Solicitors AI

Location

Hybrid – primarily remote, with in‑person collaboration once per month in Manchester or Liverpool, option for more in‑person and growing London presence

Overview

We are looking for a Fullstack Engineer to join our expanding AI team at Fletchers Solicitors. This role sits within a fast‑paced, high‑autonomy environment where we are rapidly prototyping, iterating, and deploying state‑of‑the‑art AI products for use across Fletchers and the wider legal sector. The team operates as a start‑up‑style unit within the wider business, reporting directly to the executive team, with a clear mandate to move quickly from idea to production. You will be responsible for building and maintaining the backend systems and web applications that support the development, testing, deployment, and scaling of our Machine Learning and LLM‑based tools, and for helping to transform these into robust, market‑ready products. We have ambitious plans to grow the AI team significantly over the next few years as we expand our internal capabilities and commercialise our technology externally.

About Fletchers Solicitors & the AI / Data Science Team

Fletchers is a fast-growing consumer law firm specialising in personal injury and clinical negligence, and with a growing practice in family and private client. Fletchers was one of the first consumer law firms to deploy a machine learning tool for legal work (a decision support system for screening incoming cases, launched in 2017) and was one of, or the first, law firm to have a dedicated AI department, which started in August 2023. Since then, we have been experimenting with a broader range of ML techniques, extending those tools already in use, and productionising new ones through our growing data science & engineering teams.

We believe that we are well positioned to leverage Fletchers’ unique legal‑medical dataset and industry expertise to build AI tools that will shape the future of consumer law. We are well funded through our Private Equity backers, which allows us to invest heavily in the development of sector‑specific AI tools that assist, automate, and augment our specialist legal work. Tools we have built range from simple behind‑the‑scenes custom model inference, to agentic‑AI pipelines for ‘always on’ monitoring, to the core user interface that some of our colleagues work on for 90%+ of their day. We’re also commercialising these tools so that other specialist law firms can leverage Fletchers legal and AI expertise, and have an ambitious agenda for external growth for the next 18 months.

Fletchers is headquartered in the North‑West of the UK, with offices in Manchester, Liverpool, Leeds, Southport, Bolton, Cambridge, Reading, Birmingham, Northampton, and Newcastle. With an ever‑expanding operation, it has also recently opened offices in London. Colleagues work primarily from home: the existing AI team is distributed across London, Manchester, Liverpool, Cambridge, and Bristol, and we typically meet in person once or twice per month in Manchester.

The Role

As a Fullstack Engineer within the AI team, you will support the design, development, and ongoing evolution of our core backend services, data processing pipelines, and frontend applications. You will play a key role in enabling rapid experimentation while ensuring that successful prototypes can be hardened and scaled into production‑grade systems.

You will work closely with product stakeholders, data scientists, and clients across multiple projects in parallel. This is a role suited to someone who is comfortable working close to the user, taking ownership of systems end‑to‑end, and making pragmatic engineering and architectural decisions in a fast‑moving environment.

We are open to candidates of all experience levels. The scope of responsibilities can flex depending on proficiencies and interests, with clear opportunities for rapid progression and significant professional growth for motivated candidates as the team and product portfolio grow.

Main Responsibilities

  • Take ownership of backend services and frontend applications that support the development, testing, deployment, and monitoring of ML‑enabled products
  • Contribute to infrastructure and architecture decisions by developing a strong understanding of business and product need
  • Maintain and extend existing, and build new APIs and data processing pipelines to support evolving product requirements
  • Own and maintain aspects of our frontend applications, to ensure excellent user experience
  • Collaborate closely with product and data science teams to deliver end‑to‑end solutions
  • Work directly with internal users and stakeholders to scope, prioritise, and resolve issues and bugs
  • Enable ML development through efficient and scalable data integrations from diverse sources, including case management systems, unstructured documents (Word, PDF), and SQL databases

Required Skills And Attributes

title: Shift Supervisor – Nights
description:
Shift Supervisor – Nights
White, GA | Full Time | $64,000–$68,000 based on experience

Shift: Nights, 12 hours, 6pm–6am, rotating — every other weekend required

What this job is

You'll run a night shift at our customer's rubber products manufacturing plant in north Georgia, directing one shift lead and about 20 hourly associates who keep production supplied and finished product moving. You report to the Department Manager.

This is a hands-on supervisor role. You'll spend most of your shift on the floor with your team — covering a position when someone's out, jumping on equipment when volume picks up, and staying close enough to the work to catch problems before they slow the line. The people who do well in this seat lead by working alongside their crew, not by managing from a desk.

What you'll do
  • Run shift start-up, assign work, and hand off cleanly to the next shift
  • Adjust staffing and flow so the customer's lines don't stop
  • Cover open positions and run equipment when you're short or volume spikes
  • Keep your people trained and cross-trained, and bring new hires up to speed
  • Walk the floor for safety — unsafe conditions and unsafe habits get corrected on the spot, not written up later
  • Report and document injuries, near misses, property damage, and product quality issues the same shift they happen, and secure the area until it's cleared
  • Handle attendance, performance, and conduct conversations with your team
  • Roll out process changes and make sure they hold
  • Escalate what you can't solve, and set the day shift up for success

What we're looking for

  • 2+ years running a shift, a work center, or a crew — supervisor, lead, or equivalent
  • Experience directing hourly associates in a production, warehouse, or manufacturing support setting
  • Comfortable coaching people directly, including the hard conversations
  • Able to make a call in the moment with incomplete information and stand behind it
  • Reliable on nights and weekends; the rotation is the job, not a phase
  • Forklift or material handling equipment experience preferred
  • High school diploma or GED required; degree or military experience is a plus, not a requirement

Benefits

  • Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance
  • Short-term Disability Insurance
  • Life Insurance
  • 401K + Company Match
  • Free Employee Assistance Program services and Teladoc service (24/7 telemedicine)
  • Family-Oriented Environment
